Axis coordinates
The coordinates are displayed in relation to the NCS of the job list. If the Frame option is selected, the
coordinates at the point of contact of the tool (X, Y, Z) are displayed in relation to the job frame. The angles
of the A and C axes of the machine model used are displayed.
When machines with 6 axes (3 of which are rotary axes) are used, the B axis is aligned according to the
frame defined under the following conditions:
• Frame and NCS are turned to each other
• Several orientations are possible for the rotation axes (B axis) without angle limit
• In the postprocessor configuration, the infiniteAxisFollowsFrame parameter (type: integer) is set to
1.
Simulate material removal
The material removal simulation is used to simulate complete material removal for the machining step (job)
in question, based on the currently calculated or assigned stock.
Start the material removal simulation. In this procedure,
hyperMILL analyses whether a previous calcu-
lation has generated a resulting stock model and uses this as the starting stock model. If no stock model
is present for one or more previous calculations, the Stock calculation dialogue will appear first before the
removable material simulation begins.
In the Setup area, first define the Stock and the Tolerance to be used in the material removal simulation.
Activate the Fast stock calculation option if you want to accelerate the stock generation.
Please note that models generated in this way do not show a realistic display of the milling results. This
option should therefore be preferentially used with large models for which stockmodel generation would
otherwise take a very long time.
This option is not recommended when machining prismatic components (2.5D Machining).
Furthermore, you can define in the Jobs to calculate section, for all jobs for which no resulting stockmodel
was calculated, whether these should be calculated prior to the stock removal simulation and then used as
the starting stockmodel. To do so, activate the corresponding job in the list of displayed jobs.

The Restmaterial display function can be used to display the remaining rest material after machining.
Select the required job from the job list and select Utilities → Restmaterial display from the shortcut menu.
Then, in the Stock calculation dialogue, define which stock model should be used for rest material display.
The resulting model will be displayed and the Rest material display dialogue will appear after the calcula-
tion has been carried out. Specify the parameters to display the rest material here.
The rest material analysis is also available in the Internal machine simulation!
Allowance: Allowance to be considered during rest material display.
Max. rest material: Maximum residual stock (rest material) which may be considered during rest material
display. The rest material is displayed in four steps that are defined on the basis of the value of the
maximum permissible rest material. Example: maximum rest material = 1.
First step = <0.25, second step = < 0.5, third step < 0.75, fourth step > 0.75.
Model tessellation: Accuracy of the model display ( Normal, Fine, Very fine).
After successful calculation, the colours used in the display will be shown as a colour gradient (yellow >
green > blue) in the lower left area of the dialogue.
The defined Allowance is represented by the yellow colour and the defined Max. rest material by the colour
blue.
Comparison tolerance: Sum of Model and Stock tolerance ( Simulation tolerance).
Model tolerance: Accuracy of the model used.
Simulation tolerance: Accuracy of the material removal simulation.

hyperMILL SIMULATION Center
Introduction
Use the new
hyperMILL SIMULATION Center simulation solution to check machining operations quickly
and effectively for possible collisions. After the toolpath calculation, start the simulation as follows: Right-
click and then select Simulation Center on the shortcut menu of the job or job list.
The simulation takes into account the machine defined in the Machine properties → General → Postproces-
sor dialogue and is based on the calculation of the toolpaths. This is not an NC code-based simulation.
Linking movements between individual jobs are not simulated.
The
hyperMILL VIRTUAL Machining Center software with simulation and analysis options for the NC code
after the postprocessor run is the right solution to choose if a virtual representation of the actual processes
is to be safely evaluated, controlled and optimised.
This software documentation provides information on how to use the
hyperMILL SIMULATION Center
software.
User interface
The application is adapted to the use of wide screen formats and for working with multiple screens. You
can also place variable areas outside of the program window, that is, you can move them to another
screen. When you exit a document the last window positions are saved.
The user interface consists of the following elements:

Use the main navigation toolbar to switch between the various operating modes: Project administration,
Program run (simulation), Machine configuration, VIRTUAL Machining Center configuration and Analysis.

Project administration operating mode
For extensive programs, load one of several available main programs. If the project con-
tains only one main program, this is loaded automatically.
Program run (Simulation) operating mode
Simulate the toolpath file. Display the control elements for regulating the speed, the block
display and the coordinate values. Control the display of the tool, part, stock and fixture.
Machine configuration operating mode
Control the display of the machine elements. Position the machine axes manually (manual
control). View the axis limits of the machine.
hyperMILL SIMULATION Center configuration operating mode
Set the minimum feedrate for the rapid traverse, configure the toolpath display, display the
tool reference point and coordinate systems of the machine used.
Analysis operating mode
Perform a graphical analysis of the movement paths of the machine axes, define break-
points and conditions for breakpoints, display breakpoints as a list and display breakpoint
coordinates.

In Project administration operating mode, display the main programs (VNC files), manage stock, move the
setup, define collision check options and perform a collision check.

The speed control refers to a path unit. Minimum = 0.01 mm, Maximum = 100 mm. If necessary, interpo-
lation is carried out between the individual blocks to provide a tool movement that is as uniform and
consistent as possible. If the increment is not smooth enough, blocks may also be omitted. The increment
has no influence on the collision check and material removal simulation.

as well as to moving forwards and backwards one step at a time. Double-click one of the two speed
controllers again to restore the original behaviour.

Collision check options
Use the following options to control the collision check.
The tolerance values/limit values for the still permissible contact of the tool with the
component/stock must be in reasonable proportion to the size of the tool used. OPEN
MIND recommends defining these values no larger than half the tool diameter.
hyperMILL
163

-- 163 of 1525 --

Check tool against model: Checks the tool against the model.
Check holder/shaft/core against model: Holder, shank and tool core are checked against the model.
Always check G0: The rapid traverse check is activated by default. If the Check tool against model function
is deactivated, the check for all fast travel movements can also be optionally switched off. This can make it
easier to release an NC file in certain situations (for example, when machining non-modelled areas).
Check stock: Checks tool and holder against the stock.
Remove detached stock: Only available if Check stock is enabled. If this function is activated, a check is
performed during the collision check and the simulation to see whether there is a stock area that has no
contact with the defined milling area (model). If this is the case, the stock is automatically removed during
the simulation and the collision check.
Consider core diameter for milling tools: The tool tip is checked for collisions with the stock, taking the core
diameter into account.
Limits for component contact
Use G0 tip limit / G1 tip limit to set the limit value for the still permitted contact of the tool tip with the model
in G0 and G1 movements. If a larger value is detected during the test, a message is generated.
Part allowance
Use part allowance: Activate if a part allowance should be defined for the collision check. The part
allowance is then defined either using the settings in the job (if the Use job settings option has been
activated) or it can be entered directly under Allowance. The tool shape is offset in all directions by the
entered value. If -0.01 is entered, a ball mill D10 becomes a ball mill D9.98 during the collision check.
Use job settings: Enabled by default. The values defined in the job for allowance, allowance XY and
allowance Z are used for the collision check.
A check is also performed to see whether a negative allowance or the Chamfer height
parameter is defined for theChamfer Milling on 3D Model cycle. As a component viola-
tion is desired here, no collision message is output in these cases.
If the Use job settings option has not been activated, the value for the Allowance can be entered directly.
The value that is entered is offset on the shank diameter. If -0.01 is entered, the diameter of the shank is
reduced by 0.02 (shank radius -0.01).
Only tip: The allowance is only applied to the tool tip (to be activated if, for example, only a small area at
the bottom of a cavity is to be machined with a negative allowance).
Whole tool: The stock allowance is applied to the entire tool (including thickened shank and holder) (to
be activated if, for example, a complete steep area is to be machined from top to bottom with a negative
allowance).
Stock contact
allow thin shank contact: Activate to use a tool where the shank and cutting edge have been defined
with the same diameter. The tool shank may touch the stock. No collision message is output. Use with
imprecisely defined tool geometry.
derive from stock model resolution: Activate to use a tool where the shank and cutting edge have been
defined with the same diameter. Situations in which there is a distance of 0 between the stock and shank
are not regarded as a collision. The tolerance required for the collision check is automatically derived from
the stock tolerance if the function is activated.
If the function is not activated, the value for the tolerance can be entered directly. The value that is entered
is offset on the shank diameter. If -0.01 is entered, the diameter of the shank is reduced by 0.02 (shank
radius -0.01).
hyperMILL
164

-- 164 of 1525 --

Part contact
allow thin shank contact: Activate to use a tool where the shank and cutting edge have been defined with
the same diameter. The tool shank may touch the component. No collision message is output. Use with
imprecisely defined tool geometry.
derive from job settings: Activate to use a tool where the shank and cutting edge have been defined with
the same diameter. Situations in which there is a distance of 0 between the component and shank are
not regarded as a collision. The tolerance required for the collision check is automatically derived from the
calculation tolerance in the
hyperMILL job if the function is activated.
If the function is not activated, the value for the tolerance can be entered directly. The value that is entered
is offset on the shank diameter. If -0.01 is entered, the diameter of the shank is reduced by 0.02 (shank
radius -0.01).
Tool safety distance to fixture
Safety distance to be maintained between the tool and the fixture (exception: touch probe).
Use hyperMILL settings: Use the settings from

Further collision check options
Resolution: Set the accuracy for the collision check.
Stop on first collision: During the collision check, the program stops at the first collision found.

Status messages
A status message is output, among other things:
• if a component is in collision,
• an axis is outside of the permissible limits,
• an NC block cannot be interpolated reliably and can therefore not be checked for collisions (for
example, in 180° rotations),
• a transformation is to be carried out that is not possible with the machine kinematics used.
As only the axis positions at the start and end point of a block are checked when a
VNC program file is read, a collision check must be performed in order to also display
workspace violations that arise due to the fact that an axis is located between the start
and end point of a block outside of the permissible workspace.

External simulation
hyperMILL currently supports the following external simulation programs:
• VERICUT
• COLLISION SAFEGUARD
• NCSIMUL SOLUTIONS
The following section contains information on activating and configuring external simu-
lation programs in
hyperMILL. For information on how the simulation programs work,
please consult the product documentation supplied by the respective manufacturer.
hyperMILL
180

-- 180 of 1525 --

If you use an external simulation program, you must activate it first. Afterwards, you can specify various
settings for its use.
Please note that a licence is necessary to use the program. Please contact your OPEN MIND partner for
details.
Activate VERICUT
1. First open the Application settings program.
2. Click New under Registered applications.
3. Select the VERICUT entry under Key, then go to Program, browse to the correct folder in your
VERICUT installation and select vericut.bat.
4. Confirm by selecting OK.
5. On the Postprocessor tab in the job list, select the Machine option.
6. Click the icon to open the Machine administration dialogue.
7. Define a machine whose NC output you want to check using VERICUT.
8. Activate the required simulation in the General → External simulation section.
9. Click the icon to open the configuration dialogue.
Configure VERICUT / COLLISION SAFEGUARD
Machine
Select a machine model (file format: *.mch/ *.xmhc).
Controller
Select a controller (file format: *.ctl/ *.xctl).
Project
Select a project file. This is a template file in which the VERICUT start configuration is defined (including
window view, tolerances, collision checking, etc.). To change the configuration, open the project file in
VERICUT and then save your changes.
Options
Default correction list: This value will be used if it has not already been defined in hyperMILL (job definition,
Tool tab). Numerical values (integers), variables (tool numbers) and calculation options (such as T:No+10)
may be used.
Tool reference point ID: Definition of a unique tool name (with formula support). Prerequisite for a correct
tool change.
Attach to: Specify whether the components are to be placed automatically ( Automatic option). The
VERICUT interface will then automatically search for the intended clamping position.
Position: Specify the position manually. The name of the VERICUT element at which the workpieces are
placed must be defined.
Model: Close STL specifies whether a closed solid should be created for the STL files of the model.
Option Close fixture STL creates a closed solid for the STL files of the clamping part.
Closing the files can prevent display problems in VERICUT.
Program zero: Specify whether the VERICUT interface Automatically moves the program zero point or
whether the setting is imported from the Project template.
This concludes the settings required to use the VERICUT interface.

hyperCAD
The following CAD utilities are available:
Place erroneous surfaces on layer
hyperMILL runs a plausibility check on the selected surfaces before each milling area recognition. If one
or more surfaces with errors are recognised, you can use this function to save the found surfaces with
errors to a layer.
If you start the function, the Surface error window is opened, which shows all surfaces with errors. Enter
the layer number or layer name on which the recognised surfaces are saved in the lower right input field.
Click the Move & Exit button to save the surfaces on the defined layer and to end the function. To analyse
the surfaces with errors, show only this layer. You can repair the surfaces (for example, reconstruct) or
remove them from the milling area if they are not relevant to CAM editing.
Close surfaces
You can use this function to close the (sub)surfaces of a CAD model whose boundaries lie within one
surface. If you call up the function, the newly generated surfaces have the colour that is set to active in the
CAD programme and are stored on the first available empty layer.
Split Solids
Use the Split Solid function to split solids along curves. The resulting solids remain as single solids.
First select the Solid to be cut. Then select the curve(s) that you want to use as cutting edges. Finally,
all you need to do is select the solid surface (base surface) whose normal will define the cutting direction
(direction: Normal). If you do not want to use the surface normal of the base surface as the cutting
direction, you can also define the cutting direction via Two points. You can also define colours and layers
for the resulting solids (optional).
Change entity properties
You can use this function to change the properties (layer and colour) of any elements (surfaces and
curves). First, select the elements (surfaces/curves) that you want to change. Then select the properties to
be changed ( Layer, Colour or both) and close the dialogue box.
hyperMILL

This function allows you to increase the thickness of any planes in a CAD model. Under Input, first
select the type of object selection. You can either thicken all planes of a certain colour or layer or select
the planes manually (option: Select). Afterwards, define the height and output layer of the plane to be
changed.
Export parameter
With this function, you can change parametrised CAD models by exporting a parameter list. Choose a
path and file name in order to save the content of a parameter list. Consequently, the name and value of
each parameter are saved.
Import parameter
Use this function to import changes to a parametrised model as a parameter list. Choose the Path and
File name for the current parameter list and click Open.

Produce electrodes
hyperCAD-S
hyperCAD-S Electrode offers functions for designing, managing, programming and docu-
menting complete tool electrodes with electrode holders and with product manufacturer information for
the die-sinking EDM with the spark erosion behaviour. Fully program electrodes for milling based on
hyperMILL with the electrode feature and macro programming.
Preparing milling NC programming
Various prepared tasks are to be performed. Prepare the electrode holder library. Determine default
settings. Read in the electrode colour pallet and assign the electrode colours.
Design and map the electrodes and output the electrode reports. Detailed information on this work can be
found in the
hyperCAD-S software documentation.
In the
hyperCAD-S dialogue File → Options → Electrode options → Reference → Electrode name → Incre-
ment for names, define the name of the electrode geometry and of the milling project for producing an
electrode.
Example:
Electrode name Increment for names Derived electrode geometries/
milling projects
Electrode 10 Elektrode_10.hmc,
Elektrode_20.hmc
Transfer production-related data to
hyperMILL
Production-related information such as undersize, stock size, material, areas of electrode geometry and
the position reference are mapped during the electrode design. The information in
hyperMILL is evaluated
and provided for programming.
NC Programming
NC Programming is performed semi automatically. Job list, milling area, stock, fixture and electrode
feature are automatically created in the New → Electrode milling dialogue on the shortcut menu of the
job browser. The linking of electrode feature and job, the creation of macros and the linking of electrode
features and macro are intuitively guided by the user.
Milling project directory
Define the milling project directory in the
hyperCAD-S dialogue File → Options → Electrode options →
Directories. The data for NC programming is saved in the milling project directory. This includes:

5. Feature and macro technology
The advantages of feature technology
Feature technology processes geometry information present in the CAD model for CAM programming in
a way that significantly reduces programming effort. In addition to the assigned geometry, features also
contain information relevant to manufacturing, such as tolerance values or fits.
The automatic derivation of manufacturing geometries makes it possible to transfer data directly from a
feature to the job definition (Feature Job Connector) for use across jobs and job lists.
Furthermore, Customised Process Features make it possible to define company standards for similar
geometries, thus increasing programming automation even further. In this process, work processes are
defined and stored as technology macros, which can be applied to similar machining tasks.
Feature technology provides you with enormous potential to increase efficiency and save time in manufac-
turing.
User interface
The user interface of the feature module comprises the following:
• The feature browser (Feature tab in the
hyperMILL browser) with representation of the feature lists
and features.
• The Feature editor (Feature dialogue) for defining feature parameters and
• The Feature job connector (Feature dialogue page of the job definition) for selecting and using
features in a job.

• The top area with feature lists and shortcut menu functions (1)
• The bottom area with feature and shortcut menu functions (2)
• A freely definable filter (3)
• A toolbar with filter functions and functions to control the visibility of features (4).

Generic Hole
Generic holes are universally applicable, from Simple Holes through to complex stepped holes. Generic
holes are structured according to manufacturing elements and related properties.
Generic Holes were developed to replace in the medium term the Simple Hole, Sink Hole and Free defined
Hole features.
Generic Holes offer significant advantages when using macro machining. In particular,
when setting up a macro database with macro rules, OPEN MIND recommends exclu-
sive use of Generic Holes.
Macro databases created using previous hole features do not support the new Generic Holes. The previ-
ous hole features are still supported as an option under Feature Mapping.
Geometric data from the Generic Pocket feature can be used for the 2D, 3D and drilling cycles in the job
definition.
A generic hole can contain grooves (A), sinks (B) and back sinks (3). A distinction is made between the
following basic sink types: Counterbore (1), countersink (2), drill (3), form sink (4), tapered sink (5), torus
(6) and undercut (7).

Compound Feature
Geometric data from the Compound Feature can be used for 2D, 3D, 5X and drilling cycles in the job
definition. The following parameters can be defined
Frame: Yes if uniform frame required. If this option is selected, only sub features with the same frame
system within the Compound Feature are used. No, if uniform frame is not required.
Frame origin: Enter coordinate values or determine the orientation vector from CAD system.
Frame orientation: Enter coordinate values or determine the orientation vector from CAD system.
Sub features: Select previously defined features. Existing features can be added to a Compound Feature
directly in the feature browser. To do so, select the feature and use the Compound Feature function in the
shortcut menu.
Sub features of a Compound Feature can be selected directly in the feature browser and freely moved or
reordered (drag-and-drop operations). A Compound Feature consists of referenced sub features. Changes
to one or more sub features are automatically passed to the Compound Feature.
Functions on the shortcut menu
Point optimisation:
hyperMILL optimises the paths to be travelled between the holes of the Compound
Feature. To do so, select the feature and then select the Point optimisation function from the shortcut
menu. The machining sequence is indicated by arrows. The first step is indicated by a blue arrow.
When one of the hole features within the Compound Feature already consists of several holes, these need
to be broken up first for the points to be optimised efficiently. To do so, select the feature and then select
the Explode function from the shortcut menu. The optimise the points as described above.
Reverse sequence: Use this function to reverse the machining sequence for the holes in a Compound
Feature.
hyperMILL

Sort Holes: Sort the list of intersecting holes of a Compound Feature in the feature browser. Use Diameter
or Depth to define the sort criterion. Use Ascending or Descending to determine the sort sequence Holes
that have the same diameter or the same depth are combined into a frame (feature list). If necessary,
adjust the Tolerance for the grouping.
Import hole / Export hole: Import or export all parameters defined with a hole in *.hmf format. This applies
to the Simple Hole, Sink Hole or Free defined Hole features.
Reference frame: A reference frame can be selected when exporting holes. By doing so, all holes will be
exported with their relative frame coordinates. If this option is not activated, the WCS coordinates are used
when exporting the holes. If the model position has changed, the holes will be correctly imported, if the
same Reference frame is selected.
Use feature lists: When importing the holes, you can enable the Use feature list option to preserve the
allocation of the Features to the Feature lists.

Customised Process Feature (CPF)
Use a customised process feature to perform recurring machining tasks largely automatically. Link relevant
geometric information with a machining mode and technology parameters and manually define the struc-
ture of a CPF.
Special licences are required to use the Customised Process Feature. Please contact
your OPEN MIND partner.
Requirements
To use a CPF for machining models from a family of parts that are designed in a similar way, the following
conditions should be fulfilled:
1. The models have common geometric characteristics.
2. The machining sequence is specified in the job list.
3. Geometric elements of the CPF are linked with job parameters.
Example pocket machining
Using common geometric characteristics: Profiles (1), Bottom plane (2) and Side surfaces (3), other
pockets of a part family, such as hexagonal or octagonal, flat or deep, small or large pockets, can also be
described.

Define structure
1. In the
hyperMILL browser, switch to the Feature tab.
2. Right-click and select New → Customised Process Feature → Machining object. The Customised
Process Feature dialogue opens.
3. Name the CPF according to the machining planned.
4. Specify the CPF elements to be used in the Select area.
5. Select 1 for Orientation number.
6. Click the icon to display further options. Leave the default settings Frame for Usage in job and
W (‘write’) for Mode.

Rename parameters
You can rename the parameters (for example: Orientation 1 > Frame pocket). To do this, enter the name
of your choice in the right-hand part of the line.
In addition, you can assign a graphic to each parameter that clearly shows which geometric elements
make up the parameter. This simplifies the manual selection of geometric elements in the CAD model.
Icons in the Customised process feature dialogue:
Insert graphic from a file
Paste graphic from the clipboard
Delete graphic.
Define filter
By defining a filter, you specify how elements are recognised in the CAD model. Manual assignment is
then no longer necessary. This increases the degree of automation when using the CPF.
To define a filter
1. Click the icon to open the Filter definition dialogue, select the Active checkbox and enable the
required filter option: Use colour filter, Use tag filter or Use layer filter.
2. Then click the and icons to Add / select colour filter or Add / select tag filter and define the
colour or tag class. If required, click the icon to select the surfaces that are to be used as the
basis for the filter definition.
3. If a layer filter or a layer container filter is to be used, select the Layer filter or Layer container filter
checkbox. Then click the and icons to Add / select layer filter orAdd/Select layer container
filter and define the layer/layer container.
4. To do this, in the Layer / Layer container line, click the icon / to select a layer or a layer
container that will be used for the filter definition. Click the icon to select the surfaces that are
to be used as the basis for the filter definition. By selecting sample elements, you define which
geometric elements will be used when using the CPF later on. In the case of surfaces on [Layer
2], the CPF searches in the job for surfaces that are on [Layer 2].
5. To delete one or all filters, click the Colour, Layer or Tag class line and use the Delete / Delete all
function on the shortcut menu.
6. Click the icon to include the elements found in the CAD model on the basis of the filter
definition in the selection.
Prepare CAD model
For the automatic reading of the geometry elements to work correctly using filters, the CAD models must
be created according to the filter definition.
1. Select 1 for Profile group number.
2. Click the icon and select Boundary for Usage in Job and W for Mode.
3. Enable the Milling area and Stock options and name.
4. Now confirm the CPF definition.
hyperMILL
232

The CPF structure is now completely defined. The newly created CPF appears as an entry in the list under
Customised Process Feature.
Use CPF
The aim of using the CPF is to automate extensive machining processes. Before the CPF can be used, the
data from a CAD model must be assigned. This link between the CAD model and the CPF supplies a job
with the required information when using the CPF.
Link CPF to CAD data
To link CAD data of a model to the CPF, proceed as follows:
1. Right-click the feature browser and open the CPF dialogue.
2. Select New → Customised Process Feature → [CPF name]. A corresponding entry is created in
the lower part of the feature browser [CPF name] and all previously defined geometry elements
are displayed in the CPF dialogue.
3. For Orientation 1, select the required Frame for machining.
4. Select the hub and side surfaces of the pocket for Surfaces 1 and 2.
5. Select the limit of the hub surface for Profiles 1.
6. Finally, define the Milling area and Stock.
If all parameters of the CPF are clearly named and the corresponding data from the CAD model assigned,
the CPF can be used in the job definition. The job and CPF are linked in the Feature Job Connector.
Use CPF in the job definition
Usage of a defined CPF using the example of pocket machining (roughing).
Requirements:
• All the jobs required for machining are created in the job list in the correct sequence.
• All job parameters, which are not to be taken from the CPF, are correctly defined.
To use a CPF in the job definition, proceed as follows:
1. In the job definition, switch to the Feature dialogue page and select the corresponding CPF.
2. The cycle recognises that the profile (boundary) as well as frame, milling area and stock can be
used from the CPF for roughing and automatically sets these to active. At the same time, the
corresponding parameters are "greyed out" in the job definition and cannot therefore be machined
manually.
3. Deactivate CPF parameters that are not used in the job definition. To do this, double-click the en-
try in the lower area of the Feature job connector. The status changes from Active to Deactivated.
4. The job definition is free of errors and warnings and the job can be calculated.
Reuse CPF in new CAD model
To reuse the CPF and the machining sequence with modified CAD data, proceed as follows:
1. Use the
hyperCAD-S menu File → Merge... to insert the new CAD model, which includes all
geometric elements used in the CPF.
2. Select the CPF in the feature browser, right-click and select Update filter definition(s). All ele-
ments of the CPF for which filters are defined are updated. This also applies to filters that were
not directly defined in the CPF (such as filters for the milling area).
By updating the filter, the data is read from the model and transferred to the jobs via the CPF.

Use colour table
When importing feature information from a CAD model,
hyperMILL also recognises feature properties such
as thread, ISO fits or feature classes if these are defined in a colour table.
hyperMILL evaluates the assignment of colour information to feature properties when generating features
and incorporates the corresponding parameter directly in the feature. At the same time, this parameter is
also included in the feature name and is thus available for selection when creating and using macros.
To read information from a colour table, enable the Use colour table option in the Feature Mapping
dialogue, select a file in *.xml format ( Select colour table) and confirm your entries. In order for
hyperMILL
to be able to correctly recognise the Thread and Fits feature properties, they must be defined as follows:
Example:
hyperMILL
238

-- 238 of 1525 --

<Color_Table>
<Color_Machining_Definition R="128" G="64" B="64"
FitDesignation="H7" ThreadDesignation="Mx"
FeatureClass="Special FC"
UseThreadNominalDiameter="1"/>
<Color_Machining_Definition R="128" G="0" B="128"
FitDesignation="H12"ThreadDesignation="M;G"
UseThreadNominalDiameter="0" />
</Color_Table>
The R (Red), G (Green) and B (Blue) identifiers can be assigned colour values between 0 and 255.
The FitDesignation element can assume fit designations (example H7) and the ThreadDesignation ele-
ment can assume the values M = Metric Coarse Pitch, Mx = Metric Fine Pitch, W = Whitworth and G = Gas
Uni.
Several thread types are separated by ; with the order of the list determining the order of the search.
The FeatureClass element can accept designations of defined feature classes.
UseThreadNominalDiameter can assume the values 0 and 1. 0 = Reference value is the core diameter of
the thread, 1 = Reference value is the nominal diameter of the thread.
Use colour table only: Only the holes whose colour matches the colours in the colour table are adopted.
Holes with colours, which are not defined in the colour table, are not recognised.
Use Generic Hole only: During the assignment of feature information from the CAD model, Simple Holes,
Sink Holes and Free defined Holes are transferred directly to the feature browser as Generic Holes.

hyperCAD-S should remain associatively linked
with the

defined tip angle is larger than the angle in the hole, these holes are recognised as the through hole type.
If the tip angle is smaller, the holes are recognised as the tip hole type.
Example:
(1) Min. tip angle = 75°. Holes 50°/ 60° = Through, hole 90° = Tip.
(2) Min. tip angle = 55°. Holes 50° = Through, holes 60°/90 = Tip.
(3) Min. tip angle = 45°. Holes 50°/ 60° / 90° = Tip

Feature Recognition
Interactive recognition of feature information from a CAD model. The following modules are available in
hyperMILL:
• Single Hole Recognition
• Plane Recognition
• Pocket Recognition
• Boundary Recognition
To recognise feature information from a CAD model:
1. In the
hyperMILL browser, switch to the Feature tab.
2. Right-click the upper area of the browser and select the required function from the shortcut menu.
Single Hole Recognition
Geometric information is gathered from the holes in a model by defining a sample hole and searching for
comparison holes, whose parameters are compared with the base hole.
The Single Hole Recognition dialogue comprises the following dialogue pages: Sample hole, Search and
Setup.
hyperMILL

Sample hole dialogue page
The parameters of a sample hole form the basis for recognising a hole.
Strategy
Automatic recognition: Only select a surface of the base hole. All other surfaces are automatically recog-
nised.
Manual Definition: Select all surfaces of the base hole.
Reference feature: The parameters of a reference feature are used as the basis for creating Generic Holes
based on points/circles on surfaces. On the Search dialogue page, use the Points and surfaces option
and select the surfaces/points that are to be used to create the hole features. The orientation of the newly
created hole features follows the surface normals in the area of the selected points.
Move to featurelist: Select an existing feature list to which the features will be assigned. With the New
option, a new feature list can be created.
Selection
Select surfaces of the hole.

Use the Reference feature strategy to select a feature from the list as reference features.
Parameters
List of recognised parameters of the base hole.
Further parameters can be defined if necessary.

Thread: Yes, if you want to use a Thread.

Search dialogue page
Here you can determine which hole surfaces should be compared with the base hole. As the result of this
comparison, holes are found which have the same parameters as the base hole.

You can also search for holes using the Window selection function in the CAD program.
This is particularly useful with very complex models, for which Feature Recognition is
only partly relevant.

Tolerance: The required tolerance of the curve resolution for the holes.
1

Slot tolerance: Tolerance for the axial distance (1) between concentric part-holes of the same diameter.
The following rule applies: if the distance is smaller than the tolerance, one hole is recognised (A); if the
distance is larger than the tolerance, two holes are recognised (B).
Use solid info: If the option is activated, an attempt is made to copy the direction of the drill features from
the CAD model (solid). If the option is not activated, the direction of the drill features is calculated (based
on surface information).
Use Generic Hole only: As a result of the recognition, only generic holes are created.
Pocket Recognition
The model used should be a (static) solid. Closed solids offer the strongest guarantee that all bottom
surfaces (surface normals) will be recognised correctly. In open solids, surface gaps may mean that some
topological information is missing and consequently yield incorrect results. In individual cases it may be
necessary to check the surface normals manually.
Pockets with bottoms, through pockets, open and closed pockets and T-Slots are recognised. Recognition
is performed through the use of manual or automatic surface selections.
The Pocket feature recognition dialogue comprises the dialogue pages Sample pocket, Search and Setup.
Sample pocket dialogue page
Define the pocket type to be recognised. Select the surfaces of a sample pocket. Define search options
and filter criteria. Recognised bottom surfaces and pockets are presented in a list.
Option
Pocket type: Define a pocket type for recognition purposes. Distinguish between the following:
Pocket with bottom: Pockets with a bottom are recognised.
T-Slot: T-Slots are recognised.
Pockets with bottom and T-slots: Pockets with bottom and T-slot are recognised.
Through pocket: Through pockets are recognised.
Tolerance: The required tolerance of the curve resolution for the selected feature.
Name: Define a name for the pockets. This is used in the
hyperMILL feature browser; it also contains the
smallest radius in the pocket. This name is used when performing a tool search in the macro database.
Example:
If a pocket has this name, it can be machined using tools with a radius of 3 mm or less.
hyperMILL
243

-- 243 of 1525 --

If you want pockets with bottoms to be recognised, you can use the following options to more accurately
specify the sample pockets:
Combine pockets: Enable if individual pockets of a model are to be automatically combined into a more
complex pocket.
When used in a job, combined pockets are processed more efficiently than individual pockets
It is possible to combine the following: pockets with bottoms (1), through pockets (2) and open (2) and
closed (3) pockets. The pockets must have a common edge (4) and the same frame in order to be
combined.
Pockets connected to one another through an open pocket (5) are not considered for
automatic combination.

Search dialogue page
Search for comparison pockets based on the defined sample pocket(s). Limit the search for comparison

Setup dialogue page
Limit the search using filter criteria. Define comparison parameters for the search. Define conditions for

Pocket filters
Tool diameter: Limit the pocket size using the tool diameter. Only pockets matching the following criteria
will be recognised: the upper diameter should not fit in the pocket, while the lower diameter should still fit.
Circular pocket limit: This option can be used to prevent holes from being recognized as circular pockets
by defining a diameter limitation. Only pockets that fall within the defined limitation are recognised.
Chamfer height / Fillet radius: Height of the chamfer or radius of the fillet between the bottom surface and
the pocket wall.
Chamfer angle: Lower / upper limit for the chamfer angle between the bottom surface and the pocket wall.
Allowed wall types: Specify which wall type is to be recognised. The Perpendicular option corresponds to
the Z axis of the frame that is defined on the Pocket example dialogue page.
Combine pockets: If the Suppress original pockets option is enabled, the original pockets will be deleted
after combining.
Pocket comparison parameter
These two parameters relate to the comparison between the sample pocket and the pockets that are to be
recognised (see Comparison dialogue page).
Scale limit: The minimum / maximum scale limit defines the recognition of pockets in the model on the
basis of characteristic geometric parameters.
Comparison tolerance: The degree of accuracy with which the characteristic geometric parameters (see
Scale limit) of one or more sample pocket(s) are compared with the pockets to be recognised.

Accessibility
Since not all pockets are directly accessible and can be processed, conditions for the accessibility of a
pocket are defined here.
Accessibility check: the accessibility is checked in the direction of the surface normals of the respective
bottom surfaces, and in the opposite direction (1).
Approach length: defines the minimum distance between a potential bottom plane and another surface that
may prevent access to the bottom plane (2).
1 	2
Polyhedron offset: Accessibility of the bottom plane (pocket bottom) is determined on the basis of this
contour offset over an extrusion surface. This should always be larger than the value for polyhedron
tolerance (3).
3
Polyhedron tolerance: accuracy of the polyhedron representation for the accessibility check (faceting of the
model).

value) are automatically recognised and the respective features are assigned to a corresponding feature

The name and location of the XML file can be selected freely.
Example:

Use feature
A feature defined in
hyperMILL is shown as an entry in the
hyperMILL browser and is directly available
during job definition. Two basic options are available to use a feature during job definition: from feature to
job or from job to feature.
From feature to job
To use a feature during job definition:
1. Start the
hyperMILL browser and switch to the Feature tab.
2. Select the required feature and right-click.
3. Choose the New job with feature function on the shortcut menu. A list appears with the cycles in
which you can use the selected feature.
4. Select the cycle you require and go to the Feature dialogue page.
5. The feature currently connected with the job and the status of the geometric data are displayed in
the Feature Job Connector.
To edit a feature:
1. Select the feature, right-click and select Edit.
2. Make the required changes in the Feature editor and close the editor.
To select a feature:
1. Click the icon to open the Select feature dialogue.
2. Drag the feature into the right window and confirm with OK.
In 2D cycles, only those features with the same frame as the one already being used in
the job can be added.
To change the geometry status of a feature, select the geometry to be changed in the right window, click
the right mouse button and select Active or Inactive.
If there are several geometries in the Feature Job Connector, but only one of these is to be active, select
the geometry to be changed in the right window, click the right mouse button and select Active only.
From job to feature
To use a feature during job definition:
1. Start the
hyperMILL browser, go to the Jobs tab and select the required cycle.
2. Specify the required settings and go to the Feature dialogue page.
3. Click the icon to open the Select feature dialogue.
4. Drag the feature into the right window and confirm with OK.
To define a new feature for a job,
1. right-click the left window of the Feature job connector and
2. select New → [Feature Name].
3. Select the required feature from the list.

Macro technology
Macros link machining strategies and tools for machining characteristic geometries (= features) and there-
by considerably reduce programming expenditure during production.
Advantages and uses
• Automation and recycling of workflows: Workflows can be automated and recycled using macros.
This significantly reduces programming time, particularly when it comes to producing 2.5D parts.
• Efficient macro management: Your macros reside in a macro database. This provides a production
knowledge base that is efficiently and easily managed.
• Updating workflows: You can modify your existing macros at any point to match user-specific new
production requirements as they arise.
• Higher degree of automation thanks to ‘intelligent’ macros: Using ‘intelligent’ macros, operations
that were previously assigned to a feature manually can be automatically linked. Rules and condi-
tions are defined to allow
hyperMILL to automatically decide which machining will be applied. This
method can therefore reduce the number of macros needed to machine a complete model.
Create macro
A macro includes features and job information. It is created based on a job or a feature.
Creating job-based macros
To generate a macro based on a job:
1. Open the
hyperMILL browser and select the Jobs tab.
2. Select the job that you want to associate with the macro and select Macros → New macro from
job.
The New macro window opens.
Create feature-based macro
To create a macro based on a feature:
1. Open the
hyperMILL browser and select the Feature tab.
2. Highlight the feature whose information you wish to use.
3. Right-click and select New macro from feature.
The New macro dialogue opens.
The New macro dialogue
Macro
Name: The name of the source feature. This is part of the macro name. The name is written to the macro
database when the macro is saved. The name is also used for automatic macro searches. The names of
feature-based macros contain the prefix F; the names of job-based macros contain the prefix J.
Comment: You can also enter a comment for easier identification of the macro.
Macro group: Each macro has to be assigned to a macro group. Macro groups allow you to combine
macros that are typical for a particular machining situation, for example.
Define a new macro group.
Modify a macro group.
Machine group / Material group: Enable if the macro is only to be used for one specific machine or material
group.
Define a new machine group/material group.
hyperMILL
261

-- 261 of 1525 --

Modify a machine group/material group.
Macro jobs
The bottom section of the dialogue box displays the jobs linked to the selected feature and their main tool
parameters. Click OK to save the macro in the database.
Apply macro
Apply job-based macro
In the
hyperMILL job browser, use the Macros > Apply macros function on the shortcut menu for the job.
Apply feature-based macro
In the
hyperMILL feature browser, use the Apply macros function on the shortcut menu for the feature.
Edit macro jobs
To edit a macro job, double-click the corresponding job in the macro browser or right-click and select Edit.
Editing applied jobs
To edit an applied job, double-click the corresponding job in the macro browser or right-click and select
Edit. The changes you make have no effect on the associated macro job.
Unlinking the macro job and the applied job
To deactivate the link between the macro job and the applied job, select the applied job, right-click and
then choose Unlink.
Control the display of macros in the macro browser
There are different ways of viewing macros and their associated macro jobs and applied jobs.
Click the + button or select the View → Expand function from the shortcut menu of the macro to show all
the applied macro jobs of a macro.
Select the View → Expand all function from the shortcut menu of the macro to show all the applied macro
jobs and all the applied jobs of a macro.
The Apply macro dialogue
Specify which macros should be applied in the Apply macro dialogue. Use filters to restrict or increase the
number of macros displayed. The filters differ depending on whether a job-based or a feature-based macro
is to be used.
Options
Use feature macros: When job-based macros are used, all feature-based macros are displayed.
Check geometry parameters: When job-based macros are used, only features that match the geometric
parameters of the selected feature are displayed.
Check feature class: Only features that are allocated to the same class as the selected feature are
displayed.
Check rule: Only feature-based macros, which correspond to the defined rules, are displayed.
Check frame: .When using feature-based macros, the only macros used are those which correspond to the
defined frame.
Select joblist: Available if the Check frame function is activated. The target joblist is applied to the Check
frame function.
Use tools from depot: Available for job-based and feature-based macros.
Select Depot The system searches for suitable tools with the following priority when performing a tool
search: 1.) Tool from depot, 2.) Reference tool (the tool used in the macro) and 3.) Shortest, collision-free
tool from the tool database.
Allow multiple apply: Use a feature-based macro several times.
hyperMILL

The Reverse preferred machining direction parameter enables the machining direction of the feature
applied in the macro to be reversed.
Macros
Grouping features: Group together several features with identical parameters.
Material group / Machine group: Limit display to macros that are allocated to the corresponding material
group or machine group. The left-hand side of the dialogue box differs depending on whether a job-based
or feature-based macro is used.
If a job-based macro is used, the macro group to which the macro was assigned and the number of
macros contained in this macro group are displayed.
If a feature-based macro is used, the feature upon which the macro was created and the number of
macros available for the feature are displayed.
Job list: If this function is enabled and, at the same time, machine and/or material have been defined in the
job list, the filter for machine and material will be set automatically when the macro database is opened.
The function is activated by default.
The right section of the dialogue box displays a list of all the available macros. You can enable (select
check box) or disable (clear check box) the individual macros as required.
If necessary, select the Machine group and Material group. Click Apply to apply the macro. A new entry is
created in the macro browser with the associated jobs.
Example:
(1) Macro, (2) Macro jobs, (3) Application (copy of the macro), (4) Macro jobs of the copied macro
The jobs contained in the macro are assigned to the current job list in the job browser. These jobs are
associative to the macro job. Changes to the macro job will automatically update the jobs in the macro
browser and in the job browser.
Find: Use a full-text search to search the content of the macros to find the macros suitable for machining
more quickly.
Macro jobs
All macro jobs in the database are displayed in the lower area of the Apply macro dialogue.
The macro database
A macro database is created in the
hyperMILL CONFIGURATION Center. For information, see the installa-
tion guide.
You can manage and configure your macros in the macro database. The following functions are available:
hyperMILL
263

-- 263 of 1525 --

• Save database
• Import / export macros
• Edit feature and job parameters later on
• Automatic macro search
• Optimise macros
• Specify rules for machining modes
Multi-user mode is not supported by the OPEN MIND macro database. This also applies
to macro databases with SQL Server technology.
To open a database:
1. In the
hyperMILL browser, go to the Macros tab.
2. Right-click and select View Macro DB.
User interface
The user interface of the macro database consists of the following elements:
1. The top section (left window) displays the defined macro groups as well as the number of macros
contained in these groups (right window).
2. The top right window lists the macros contained in these macro groups.
3. The bottom window displays the macro jobs linked to the individual macros alongside their most
important tool parameters.
Macro groups
Control the display of the macros in a macro group by activating/deactivating a macro group. The Number
column displays the number of macros contained in a macro group.
hyperMILL
264

-- 264 of 1525 --

Macros
The list view displays the macro name as an abbreviation of the feature or job parameters with the name
affix ( F) for feature or ( J) for job.
Macro jobs
The list displays only the macro jobs that are contained in the macro that is selected in the upper window
of the database.
Save macros
Click Save to save a newly created or updated database. The macros contained in the database are saved
in *.mdb format in the following directory:
C:\Users\Public\Documents\OPEN MIND\mac\
Import / export macros
You can export single macros or all the macros in a database, or you can import macros into the existing
database from another database.
To export all the macros of a macro database:
1. Click Export all and enter a file name or
2. click File and select an existing file in *.omx format (OPEN MIND Exchange Format).
To export individual macros:
1. Highlight the respective macros in the right-hand window and click Export selected.
2. Click File and select an existing file in *.omx format (OPEN MIND Exchange Format).
To import macros from another database:
1. Click Import → macros.
2. Select the respective file in *.omx format (OPEN MIND Exchange Format).
Edit macro parameters
You can change the names of macro groups, job parameters and macro parameters in the macro data-
base. This way, you can react quickly and flexibly to changes in the conditions.
Macro group: To change the name of a macro group, double-click the corresponding list entry.
Macro parameter: When you double-click the macro entry in the list, the macro's main parameters are
displayed in a separate overview window. Double-click the feature parameters/values in this window to edit
them.
Job parameters: To change job parameters, highlight the required macro job in the bottom window of the
database and click Edit or double-click the corresponding list entry.
Confirm your changes and close the dialogue.
Changes do not take effect until you have clicked Save to update the changes in
the database. Changes to macros in the database have no effect on macros already
applied in the job browser or macro browser.
hyperMILL
265

-- 265 of 1525 --

Conversely, editing the applied macros has no effect on the macros stored in the database.
Create new macro group
To create a new macro group, right-click the left window and select New.
Move macro
To move a macro to another macro group, right-click the macro you want to move in the right window,
select Move to...> and select the macro group to which you want to move the macro.
Delete macro group
To delete a macro group, right-click the macro group you want to delete in the left window and select
Delete.
Delete macros
To delete a macro, right-click the macro you want to delete in the right window and select Delete.
Copy macros
To copy a macro, right-click the macro you want to copy in the right window and select Copy.
Copy and paste macro jobs
Use the Job/ Copy all jobs to clipboard function on the shortcut menu of the macro job to copy one or all
macro jobs from a macro. Use the Paste job / Paste all jobs function on the shortcut menu of the macro job
to paste the copied job/jobs into another macro.
Tools in the macro database
The Tool data column in the list view indicates how the used tool was created. A distinction is made
between the following:
Macro: The tool was defined directly in the macro (or job) without a search of the tool database.
DB: the tool used for the job is taken from the tool database (numbered NC tool).
DB+Auto: Only applies to 2D drilling jobs. Like DB + automatic tool search, the Tool length is taken into
account. All of the tools suggested are collision-free.
DB+Auto+: Only applies to 2D drilling jobs. Like DB + automatic tool search, the Tool length and Tool
diameter are taken into account. All of the tools suggested are collision-free.
Automatic macro search
During an automatic macro search,
hyperMILL searches the database for macros that match the selected
feature and then applies these.
Macro optimisation
Jobs that can be machined using the same tool are processed in sequence (tool change optimisation).
Intelligent macros
Macros link machining strategies and tools with geometric information. Intelligent macros also include rules
that evaluate geometric information and define when a machining strategy is executed. Intelligent macros
are available for all types of features.
hyperMILL
266

-- 266 of 1525 --

Initial situation: The workpiece to be machined contains many holes of various depths, diameters and sink
types. A typical procedure in production may then be as follows:
1. Using Feature Mapping, the drilling geometries are recognised automatically and saved as a
feature.
2. The assignment of the machining methods of these features (jobs) and the saving as a macro are
initially done manually.
3. The rules are now defined in the next step. They determine which part of a macro is to be
executed under specific conditions.
Define rule
To define a rule for an intelligent macro:
1. Open the macro database and select the macro for which you wish to define a rule.
2. Right-click and select Free feature parameter.
3. Specify the parameters you want to free. When you do this, the link between feature parameters
and macros is severed so that you can then use the parameters for the purpose of rule definition.
4. Now open the job to which you wish to assign a rule by double-clicking the job entry in the lower
area of the macro database (macro jobs).
5. On the Rule dialogue tab, click the Job active entry and then click the icon .
6. Set the conditions for enabling a machining mode (of a job) based on simple IF-THEN rules.
A part of the macro name is then displayed in square brackets (example: F:D8[Through]). This indicates
that parameters have been freed.
Feature parameters and formulas can be used to define macro rules.
With the aid of formulas, tool parameters (such as T:Rad, T:Len, T:GageLen, T:Ti-
pAng) and user variables (such as F:H, F:R, F:LD) are available for rule definition.
Once you have confirmed your entries, the job will be marked in the macro database with [R] = Rule.
Example: [R] Simple Drilling.
hyperMILL
267

-- 267 of 1525 --

If all geometries in the model and strategies necessary for machining have been specified as part of the
rules and if the corresponding macros have been saved in the macro database, they will be available for
cross-model application.
Upon application of the macros,
hyperMILL automatically provides for each geometry the correct machin-
ing sequence and thus enables the automatic machining of the models to be machined.
Copy and paste rule
Use the Copy rule to clipboard / Paste rule functions on the macro shortcut menu to copy and paste macro
rules between different macro jobs.
Functions on the shortcut menu: Macros
Update macro from database: Update the selected macro with the parameters from the macro database.
Save changes to database: Save the parameters of the selected macro to the macro database.
View macro database: Display the macro database.
Calculate: Calculate the toolpath(s) for the selected job(s).
Internal simulation...: Simulate the toolpath using the internal simulation.
Set toolpath status: Check whether the toolpath is still current for the geometry.
Toolpaths >
Show / Hide / Autoshow / Delete: Show, hide, automatically display or delete the toolpaths of the selected
job.
Check model: Check the consistency of the contours assigned to the job.
Delete: Delete the selected macro.
View >
Expand / Collapse: Hide or show the jobs linked to the selected macro.
Expand all / Collapse all: Show or hide all the jobs in the macro browser.

268

-- 268 of 1525 --

6. Probing
Available machining cycles
3D Point Probing: Measure the coordinates of any 3D points to measure the accuracy of a machining job.
Workpiece alignment along edge: Compensation of a workpiece misalignment with a probing tool along an
edge. The compensation angle is calculated automatically by
hyperMILL, which means there is no need to
manually align the fixture.
Workpiece alignment with holes: Compensation of a workpiece misalignment with a probing tool using two
holes. The compensation angle is calculated automatically by
hyperMILL, which means there is no need to
manually align the fixture.
Rectangular Probing: Measure the size and location of rectangular bosses and pockets to measure the
accuracy of a machining job. Optionally, a reference tool can be adjusted and the origin can be set.
Slot-Rib Probing: Probing of the size and position of slots and ribs with the option to adjust a reference tool
and set the origin.
Circular Probing: Measure the size and location of cylinders and holes to measure the accuracy of a
machining job. Optionally, a reference tool can be adjusted and the origin can be set.
Axis dependent Probing: Measure the location of points depending on the X, Y and Z axis of the machining
frame to measure the accuracy of a machining job. Optionally, a reference tool can be adjusted and the
origin can be set.
hyperMILL
269

-- 269 of 1525 --

3D Point Probing
Probing of point(s) on any surface/model. The motion of the probe is perpendicular to the touch point.
The results are the coordinate of the probe in X, Y and Z when it triggers. Evaluation of the deviation is
performed via protocol.
X
Z
Tools
Permissible tool types are touch probe tools. The geometry parameters correspond to the geometry
parameters of the lollipop tool type. Possible tool reference points are Tip and Centre.
Contours
Probing mode
Automatic (1): Select when the probing direction is to be detected automatically.
Manual (2): The probing direction can be set manually for individual probing points. To do this, activate
under Contour attributes the required points and the Reverse option.
1 2
Contour selection / faces
Select Points and Surfaces. The points to be measured must be located on the selected
surfaces.
Offset: If there is an allowance on the model to be measured, define a corresponding offset for the
measuring points.
hyperMILL
270

-- 270 of 1525 --

Parameters
Infeed
Infeed length (1): Length of the toolpath at the feedrate to the surface contact of the ball of the probing
tool.
Additional infeed length : Added to the infeed length in the component direction to ensure that the touch
probe contacts the component. This should be used in particular in cases with a negative offset (electrode
machining).
1
Tolerances
Symmetric: Lower allowance and upper allowance are the same. Use Tolerance -/+ to define the mini-
mum/maximum permissible deviation of the actual dimension to the target dimension.
Two sides: Define Lower allowance and Upper allowance. The values may be different.
NC
Create log file: Creates a measuring log.
Select Default if the machine is to create a measuring log with the structure specified by OPEN MIND. Use
the Extra function to generate a measuring log that can be customised.
The Best Fit and Best Fit verification functions are only available with an appropriate
licence.
The Best Fit function (only 3D Point Probing) generates a measuring log that can be read in with the
hyperMILL VIRTUAL Machining Center. The measuring log contains the position values on the component
that is not yet aligned.
In
hyperMILL VIRTUAL Machining Center, the measuring log is read in and the actual component position
is calculated.
The real position determined in
hyperMILL VIRTUAL Machining Center is finally verified using the Best Fit
verification function so that safe machining can take place on the machine.
For further information on the Best Fit function, also see the
hyperMILL VIRTUAL Machining Center
product documentation.
Stop program if out of tolerance: Stop measuring if a measured value is outside of the specified tolerance
range.

Some controllers do not support automatic log generation/Message mode. Please con-
tact your OPEN MIND partner if you have any questions.
Retract mode
Defines the Z level where retract movements are executed.
Safety distance/ clearance plane: All retract movements are executed via the clearance distance/clearance
plane. .
Clearance
Security plane: Specify the level of the security plane.
Axial clearance/lateral clearance: Minimum distance in an axial or lateral direction from the surface of the
model.
Reposition feedrate: Feedrate of the tool during the repositioning between two measurements.
Setup
Model
Specify the model (milling area) required for the current job.
For further information, see section Prepare manufacturing geometry (page 60).
Additional surfaces: Temporary safety surfaces to avoid unnecessary rapid travel movements. Surfa-
ces in the machining area that need to be known to perform a correct collision check.
Check tool
The tool check ensures that all of the components defined for the tool are protected from a possible
collision with the CAD model on the basis of existing material. The tool check is only available if you have
defined a tool and also a model to be checked.
Check on: You must always enable this option if you want the tool to be checked for collisions. If the tool
check is not enabled, the tool used is shown in red in the graphic preview. When this check is enabled,
the defined clearance is used to check all of the components defined for the tool. We recommend that you
define the clearance so that it gets continuously larger, starting with the thick shank in the direction of the
spindle.
Tool check setup: the tool check settings are specified in this dialogue box. For further information, see
section Tool check setup (page 768)
NC parameters
Machining tolerance: Enter the required tolerance. The value defines the accuracy with which the calcula-
tion for the generation of toolpath is carried out.
Stop before execution: A stop marker in the toolpath causes the tool to stop.

OPEN MIND recommends that you proceed as follows for the workpiece alignment:
1. Define the approximate zero point position of the workpiece.

dependent Probing cycles.
Tools
Permissible tool types are touch probe tools. Possible tool reference points are Tip and Centre.
Contours
Select contour
Contour: Select an edge (1) or two points (2) that are to be used for probing. The direction of the
contour determines the sequence of the probing process. The start point, end point and direction of the
contour defined in this way are displayed as graphical feedback. Select Reverse to reverse the direction of
the contour.

values result in an inwards movement and negative values result in an outwards movement.
Mode

7. Turning
Turning is a production process for manufacturing rotationally symmetrical internal and external surfaces
by removing material from turning stock of any shape. The external shape of a workpiece is created by
using the Outside option, and the internal shape by using the Inside option.
The
millTURN module allows for the combination of milling and turning tasks in a job list.
Stockmodel for subsequent machining tasks: As with milling jobs, a stockmodel can also be generated for
subsequent turning operations (resulting stock).
NC files: The NC files created with the
millTURN module can be used for both milling and turning tasks.
Available machining cycles
Roughing: Roughing of turning stock of any shape in axial or radial machining direction.
Contour parallel Turning: Roughing of turning stock of any shape parallel to contour.
Finishing: Contour parallel finishing of workpieces of any shape based on a preceding roughing operation.
Rollfeed Turning: Machining of workpieces by rolling the tool insert on the component contour, ensuring a
very high surface quality.
3X simultaneous Roughing: Roughing of workpieces with a simultaneous swivel axis.
3X simultaneous Finishing: Finishing of workpieces with a simultaneous swivel axis.
Groove Turning: Axial roughing of workpieces with grooves or shoulders.
Groove Plunging: Radial roughing of workpieces with grooves and shoulders.
Groove Finishing: Radial finishing of turning workpieces with grooves or shoulders.
Face Groove Turning: Radial roughing of workpieces with axial oriented grooves or shoulders. The tools
used normally have three cutting edges.
Face Groove Plunging: Axial roughing of workpieces with axial oriented grooves or shoulders. The tools
used normally have three cutting edges.
Face Groove Finishing: Finishing of workpieces with axial oriented grooves or shoulders.
Parting: Radial machining to separate the component from the bar stock, optionally with chamfer. Parting
off can be done on the front or at the back of the workpiece.
Thread Cutting: Creation of single or multiple start, cylindrical or conical, external and internal threads with
constant pitch. Infeed can be performed either with constant chip section or with constant X value.

Auto-creating a contour
Use Feature → 2D Contour to automatically derive the appropriate contour for a machining operation
(roughing, grooving, etc.) from the contour of the turning model.
Procedure:
1. Create the contour for the turning model as Feature → 2D contour.
2. Create a turning job for the desired machining operation (such as grooving) and navigate to the
Feature dialog page.
3. Select the Feature 2D Contour created in the first step and double-click to move it to the window
on the right.
4. The part of the contour of the turning model used for machining is automatically set to Active and
displayed to provide graphical feedback.
Example (1) Turning stock contour, (2) Turning model contour
(A) Roughing, (3) Turn contour outside, (4) Turn contour plane
(B) Groove Plunging, (5) Groove contour outside
(C) Face Groove Turning, (6) Groove contour front plane
(D) Parting, (7) Parting back face

Parameters
Infeed
Radial / axial infeed to the next machining plane.
Constant (1): Constant infeed depth over the entire machining area.
Ascending (2): Based on a starting infeed (a) the infeed value is increased by one value per cut. The
Maximal cutting depth (b) prevents infeed depths that can cause tool breakage.
Descending (3): Based on a starting infeed (a) the infeed value is increased by one value per cut. The
Minimal cutting depth (b) prevents infeed depths that are too small.
Ramp (4): The infeed alternates between tapered and horizontal. By defining the infeed (a) and the
minimal cutting depth (b), the ramp angle is calculated automatically in relation to the contour.

High Performance Roughing
Use if material that is difficult to cut is to be machined or a reliable chip break cannot be achieved with

hyperMILL MAXX Machining for turning jobs is characterised by:
• High degree of process reliability and material removal plus a high level of quality at the same time.
• Constant, low load on the tool and machine during the entire machining.
• Support for round inserts.
• Feedrate for fast positioning movements.

Strategy
Linear: (1), (2) Material is removed parallel to the turning axis in accordance with the specified Infeed
direction (see Strategy dialogue page).
Ramping: (3), (4) Ramp-shaped material removal. Here, a ramp-shaped first cut is always made on a
plane and the remaining material is cleared on the same plane in a second cut parallel to the turning axis.
Zigzag: (2), (4) Machining with alternating cutting mode.

Fillet radius: Additional toolpath filleting in the corners. Default: corner radius * 0.1.
Feedrate
Feedrate reposition: Feedrate for the repositioning between the infeed planes.
Unit: mm or inch/revolution of the workpiece.
Tool life control
Activate the function if the material to be machined requires the time the tool is engaged to be controlled.
Use the Distance option and the Max. Distance parameter to define the maximum permissible length of the
toolpath for which the tool is engaged. Select the Time option in order to define the maximum permissible
time for which the tool should be engaged using the Max. time parameter. Number of paths limits the
time the tool is engaged with the Max. number of paths parameter. When the defined condition has been
achieved, the machining ends and the tool retracts to the clearance plane.

Ramp (4): Define ramp length and ramp angle.

Turning stock
Turning stock is defined on the basis of a closed, planar contour in the X-Z plane of the turning frame and
the associated turning axis in the X-Z plane.
Open the Stock model dialogue. Specify a name and, if necessary, a comment for the turning stock.
Enable a mode that is to be used to create the turning stock.
Generate turn resulting stock: Create a stock model for subsequent turning jobs based on the current
turning job. The stock model is named after the job that was used to create it.
Generate mill resulting stock: Create a stock model for subsequent milling jobs based on the current
turning job or a combination of milling and turning jobs.
From existing mill stock: Select base stock from which a mill resulting stock is to be created.
The From existing mill stock option should only be used if the following conditions are
fulfilled:
1. Prerequisite: mill/drill machining with non-rotationally symmetrical removal.
2. The milling job begins when the turning job is complete.
If these conditions are not fulfilled, computing times may increase as a result of different
resolutions during stock tracking.
Generate milling stock from turning stock: Any turning stock that is represented by an entry in the
hy-
perMILL model browser can be used to create a milling stock model.

from the shortcut menu. Specify the required resolution and click OK to confirm. The created milling stock

hyperMILL model browser.

turning area (turning model) and the turning stock must lie in the X-Z plane.

Infeed
Constant (1): Constant infeed depth over the entire machining area.
Ascending (2): Based on a starting infeed (a) the infeed value is increased by one value per cut. The
Maximal cutting depth (b) prevents infeed depths that can cause tool breakage.
Descending (3): Based on a starting infeed (a) the infeed value is increased by one value per cut. The
Minimal cutting depth (b) prevents infeed depths that are too small.
Ramp (4): The infeed alternates between tapered and horizontal. By defining the infeed (a) and the
minimal cutting depth (b), the ramp angle is calculated automatically in relation to the contour.

Machining mode
Limit machining to selected areas.
Flat and steep areas are separated from each other by a slope angle. 0° corresponds to parallel to the
turning axis and 90° is perpendicular to the turning axis.
Off: Steep and flat areas of the defined contour are machined (1).
Steep areas: Only the steep areas of the defined contour are machined (2).
Flat areas: Only the flat areas of the defined contour are machined (3).

Models and stock models for turning cycles are always shown in a 2D view for the sake

Turning model
A turning model is defined on the basis of a closed, planar contour that is located in the X-Z plane of the
turning frame.
hyperMILL
346

-- 346 of 1525 --

Collision check: If this option is selected, the holder of the tool used is permanently checked for potential
collisions against the current stock model (tracked stock model) and the current turning model.
Open the Turning area dialogue. Specify a name and, if necessary, a comment for the turning area.
Generate a turning area by selecting a closed contour.
Open the Create turning area from model dialogue to create a turning area from surfaces or solids.
Define the frame, colour and layer of the turning contour.
Frame for turning axis
Select a frame for the turning axis from the list.
Define the Colour and Layer of the turning contour. Select Use model colours to adopt the current colours
from the model.
Surfaces
Resolution: Define the resolution (fineness) of the turning area.
Select surfaces or a solid.
hyperMILL automatically creates a turning contour that defines the turning
area. An entry is created in the
hyperMILL browser and a Contour feature is created in the feature
browser.
Turning stock
Turning stock is defined on the basis of a closed, planar contour in the X-Z plane of the turning frame and
the associated turning axis in the X-Z plane.
Open the Stock model dialogue. Specify a name and, if necessary, a comment for the turning stock.
Enable a mode that is to be used to create the turning stock.
Generate turn resulting stock: Create a stock model for subsequent turning jobs based on the current
turning job. The stock model is named after the job that was used to create it.
Generate mill resulting stock: Create a stock model for subsequent milling jobs based on the current
turning job or a combination of milling and turning jobs.
From existing mill stock: Select base stock from which a mill resulting stock is to be created.
The From existing mill stock option should only be used if the following conditions are
fulfilled:
1. Prerequisite: mill/drill machining with non-rotationally symmetrical removal.
2. The milling job begins when the turning job is complete.
If these conditions are not fulfilled, computing times may increase as a result of different
resolutions during stock tracking.
Generate milling stock from turning stock: Any turning stock that is represented by an entry in the
hy-
perMILL model browser can be used to create a milling stock model.
Highlight the corresponding turning stock model in the browser and select the Create milling stock function
from the shortcut menu. Specify the required resolution and click OK to confirm. The created milling stock
model appears as an entry in the
hyperMILL model browser.
Frame: The Z axis of the machining frame must be the same as the rotary axis of the tool. Both the
turning area (turning model) and the turning stock must lie in the X-Z plane.
