MB Point Milling
The cycle supports multiple processor cores and therefore shows a significant performance improvement
for large calculations.
Strategy
The blade surfaces are machined in a continual, spiral-shaped and circumferential movement with tool
point contact. Point milling should preferably be used if the blade surfaces are twisted double to such an
extent that it is not possible to perform flank milling.
Milling reference
Main blade / Splitter blade: Specify the blade you want to machine. The selection of the splitter will not be
available, if it has not been defined on the geometry model.
Pocket mode
Activate: As an alternative to the familiar continuous machining around the selected reference main blade,
here the machining of the main blades takes place in the pocket, with the right-hand surface of the left
blade and the left-hand surface of the right neighbour blade being machined in one operation.
The advantage of this machining strategy is that aids for reducing vibration can be introduced in the
neighbouring pockets.
Entry position
Leading side / Trailing side: You can machine either on the leading (1) or trailing edge (2). When machin-
ing with the zigzag strategy, you should preferably start at the upper edge. With a constant machining
direction, the entry position is generally dependent on the best possible lead angle.
Infeed strategy
Parallel to hub: The profile of the toolpaths is based on the hub. Constant path distance.
Compared to flow-strategy machining, the machining time is generally shorter given the same maximum
infeed.
hyperMILL
1364

-- 1364 of 1525 --

Flow: The profile of the toolpaths on the blades follows the direction of the flow. The path distance on the
blades changes continually where the edges are of a different length.
Compared to partial cutting, it takes longer to machine with the same maximum infeed. As the milling
grooves follow the direction of the flow, a greater scallop height and therefore a greater path distance may
be permissible.
Parameters
Machining area in the axial direction
The top and bottom limits for the axial machining area are defined differently according to the selected
infeed strategy (see the strategy panel).
Infeed strategy: Flow
The top and bottom limits are defined using iso parameters:
• The maximum permissible value for the top limit’s iso parameter = 1.
• The minimum permissible value for the bottom limit’s iso parameter = 0.
Partial machining jobs can be performed by correspondingly selecting the iso parameters.
hyperMILL
1365

-- 1365 of 1525 --

Complete machining Iso parameter (top limit) = 1.
Iso parameter (bottom limit) > 0.
Iso parameter (top limit) < 1.
Iso parameter (bottom limit) > 0.
The machining job always start with an open spiral.
The machining job end with:
• Closed spiral if the iso parameter for the lower limit is 0.
• Open spiral if the iso parameter for the lower limit does not equal 0.
It is possible to force an open spiral on the lower limit using a very small value (approx. machining
tolerance).
Consecutive machining jobs will fit together ideally if
• the hub allowance is not changed in a series of partial machining,
• the tool diameter is not changed.
In the case of consecutive machining jobs, smooth lead-in/fade-out ensures that different deflections and
tool tolerances do not appear on the blade surfaces.
Additional overlapping paths
• may be specified above (upper limit < 1) and below (lower limit > 0),
• extend the machining area by the user-defined number of paths and
• continuously decrease/increase the distance from/to the blade surfaces.
Infeed strategy: Parallel to the hub
Top limit
Defines the Entry start height for partial machining.
When Manual hub offset is not defined: The blade is machined completely.
Manual hub offset: The value should correspond to the hub allowance from the previous machining job
(point milling).
hyperMILL
1366

-- 1366 of 1525 --

Manual hub offset not defined Manual hub offset defined
Consecutive machining jobs will fit together ideally if
• the tool diameter is not changed,
• the entered value corresponds to the hub allowance of the previous machining job.
In the case of consecutive machining jobs, smooth lead-in/fade-out ensures that different deflections and
tool tolerances do not appear on the blade surfaces.
Additional overlapping paths above (manual limit defined):
• extend the machining region by user-defined number of paths
• continuously reduce the distance to the blade surface from a user-defined value.
Lead out paths below (manual limit defined)
• reduce the cutting load for the defined number of final paths before the hub allowance (no extension
below the offset to bottom surfaces),
• increase the distance relative to the blade surface to a user-defined distance.
Technology: Edge behaviour
Leading edge feedrate / Trailing edge feedrate
You can define a local feedrate for both edges to prevent the rotary axes from acceleration too quickly
around these edges.
Technology: Final paths
If the pre-machining job used a larger tool, this may mean that more material is left in the transition radius
between the blade and hub surface.
5 axes
Inclination strategy
4X Machining: Depending on the blade geometry, it may be possible to calculate a fixed tilt for the second
rotary axis. Access is then solely achieved by rotating about the Z axis.
Avoidance strategy
Around Z: This option activates the previously used behaviour, where the collision avoidance is mainly
implemented by pivoting around the Z-axis.
Advantage: Very simple movement of the tool that can lead to constant speed of the rotary axes.
Camberline: This option activates a new strategy for collision avoidance that is mainly implemented
perpendicular to the camberline (centreline) of the blade.
Special options
Close to blade: Facilitates precise tool control near to the blade with optimised inclination and the lowest
possible number of axis movements on the machine.
hyperMILL
1367

-- 1367 of 1525 --

Precise avoidance: If this option is enabled, the mesh for collision avoidance will be calculated with approx.
20% greater accuracy than for point calculation of the toolpath, so that even a tool positioned vertically at
the blade can typically move without collision between two long and closely placed blades.
Edge behaviour
Min. angle - leading edge / Min. angle - trailing edge: Minimum angle that must be maintained on the
leading or trailing edges. This helps to optimise the machining of different edge shapes.
Intermediate angle down / Intermediate angle up
Angle to Z: Defined angle of the tool to the Z axis for downwards and/or upwards movement at the critical
location, usually between the main blade and the leading edge on the splitter
Iso position (from leading) / Iso position (from trailing): Specify the location where the angle defined relative
to the Z axis is to be placed. The advantage of this method is that you may be able to use tools that are
better suited for working in the small spaces between the blades. This allows you to increase the process
parameters and thus reduce the machining time.
Frame angle limitation
Max. angle to Z: The frame angle limitation prevents the system from calculating a tool orientation that the
machine cannot carry out.
Macros
Approach macro / Retract macro
The approach and retract movement is performed in a quarter circle. Define radius.
Axial feedrate
Feedrate: Feedrate for the macro movement in axial direction.
Link macro
Only for Parallel to hub strategy. The link macro connects the toolpaths of both flanks – which are trimmed
against the shroud. The Height (1) and Radius (2) define how the link movement is performed over the
shroud.
Split paths: During 4X Machining, continuous machining around the blade can be obtained by automati-
cally splitting the paths at both edges and connecting these paths again with an additional macro. The
advantage is that you can use tools with cone angles on 4-axis machines that would have damaged the
edge(s) using uninterrupted circumferential machining. This allows you to increase the process parameters
and thus reduce the machining time.

MB Flank Milling
Strategy
Circumferential, swarf cut machining of blade surfaces.
The cycle should preferably be used when the blade surfaces allow for sufficiently accurate tool fit to
surface. Compared to point milling, this cycle thus achieves shorter machining times.
Requirements:
• The blade surfaces must be regular surfaces.
• The selected blade surfaces should not contain a transition radius to the hub.
• You must select the trim curves to the left and right of the edge.
Milling reference
Main blade / Splitter blade: Specify the blade you want to machine. The selection of the splitter will not be
available, if it has not been defined on the geometry model.
Entry position
The approach generally takes places on the edge that is not rounded (normally the trailing edge). Howev-
er, the given space must also be taken into account.
Infeed strategy
This option is only important if you want to perform several infeeds in the axial and lateral direction.
Axial infeed first: All infeeds in the axial direction are carried out for each lateral layer before the next
lateral infeed occurs.
Side infeed first: All lateral infeeds are carried out for each axial layer before the next axial infeed occurs.
To protect the cutting tool, you can optionally define an axial retract for every lateral infeed.
Edge Milling
The following options are available for machining the blade edges:
None: There is no machining of the blade edges. No edge surface(s) is/are selected at the start position
(usually the blunt edge) and the edge distance is > 0.
Enclosed edge only: Only the enclosed blade edge is machined. No edge surface(s) is/are selected at the
start position (usually the blunt edge) and the edge distance is 0.
Both: Both (round) blade edges are machined.
Parameters
Allowance
Hub allowance / Blade allowance: Remaining minimum allowance on the hub surface / blade surface.
Axial infeed
Manual stepdown: If the axial infeed is not limited manually, the system will only calculate one infeed in the
axial direction. When specifying a maximum axial stepdown, the number of axial steps will be calculated
from the height of the blade.
Lateral infeed / infeed strategy
Side width: In the lateral direction, the thickness of the material defines the machining area. The number of
paths is derived from the lateral infeed.
Technology: edge behaviour
If the option Parameter → Edge Milling → None is activated, the following functions are available:
Edge clearance (1): The tool is moved around the edge (1) with the defined distance.
Edge lift (2): You can avoid damaging this surface by entering an additional clearance distance relative to
the hub in the edge area (2).
hyperMILL
1372

-- 1372 of 1525 --

Feedrate: Define the feedrate for edge rolling.
If the option Parameter → Edge Milling → Enclosed edge only is activated, the following functions are
available:
Feedrate: Define the feedrate for edge rolling.
If the option Parameter → Edge Milling → Both is activated, the following functions are available:
Overlap length: (1) Define the length of the overlap of the toolpaths in the blade edge area (leading edge).
Overlap distance: (2) Define the maximum height of the lifting movement during the overlap.
Feedrate: Define the feedrate for edge rolling.

Technology: Final paths
If the pre-machining job used a larger tool, this may mean that more material is left in the transition radius
between the blade and hub surface.
Using this feature, you can define technology values for a Path number which meet the requirements for
this increase in material removal.

Technology: Compensation spring path
Compensation path: Milling forces may cause the tools and blades to bend, resulting in defects in the form.
One way to compensate spring paths is to repeatedly mill the last path. It is duplicated automatically if the
feature is enabled. You can define the feedrate and RPM for this toolpath separately.
5 axes
Inclination strategy
Automatic: Automatically calculates the best fit of the tool to the blade surface, deviating from the ISO
lines.
Additional angle leading edge / Additional angle trailing edge: Manual definition of the tool’s lead angle by
the leading and trailing edge. A linear interpolation is performed between both values relative to the blade
surface’s ISO lines.
Blade tolerance
Blade tolerance defines the required blade accuracy – even around enclosed edge.
Machining tolerance must be 5 to 10 times more accurate than the blade tolerance.
Upper limit: defines the max. oversize around the blade.
Lower limit: hardcoded max. undersize (symmetric tolerance band).
Clearance angle: entry position
Clearance angle: entry position controls the tool axis at the entry position at both sides optionally and
independent to each other. Positive values lean the tool toward outside. To be applied to reduce the total
amount of tilting or to avoid pole transition.
Frame angle limitation
Max. angle to Z: The frame angle limitation prevents the system from calculating a tool orientation that the
machine cannot carry out.
Macros
Approach macro/Return macro
Length: Length for tool approach and retract movements.
Additional axial distance: Increases the approach and retract path of the macros in the tool axis direction.
Axial feedrate
Feedrate: You can define the feedrate for the macro movement in the axial direction separately. It is
usually preferable to use a higher feedrate here.

MB Edge Milling
Strategy
Milling reference
Main blade / Splitter blade: Specify the blade whose edge you want to mill. The selection of the splitter will
not be available, if it has not been defined on the geometry model.
Edge
Leading edge / Trailing edge: Specify the edge you want to machine.
Infeed strategy
Zigzag: Machining with alternating orientation.
Oneway: Edge milling starts in the centre above the edge surface. Material is always removed using climb
milling.
To ensure climb milling can be performed, the material is removed as follows:
• In the area left of centre, material is removed (from the hub to the shroud) with a drawing cut.
• In the area right of centre, material is removed (from the shroud to the hub) with a plunging cut.
The lift off paths are performed with feedrates that can each be defined separately using a given clearance
distance parallel to the cutting toolpath.
hyperMILL
1377

-- 1377 of 1525 --

Parameters
Technology: Smooth overlap
Overlapping paths, Final distance: According to the number specified, the system generates additional
paths on each side at the transition to the flank surfaces. These additional paths are created with lateral
distance that increases in relation to these flank surfaces. This reduces the cutting force and therefore the
tool deflection.
In the case of consecutive machining jobs, this smooth fading out prevents different deflections and tool
tolerances from appearing on the blade surfaces. You generally need to keep the values you enter for the
number of overlapping paths and final distance very small.
Technology: Opening cut
Path number: If a lot of material is still left on the edge, it is possible to make additional opening cuts to
avoid overloading the tool.
Material height: The infeed between the opening cuts is calculated from the specified material height (of
the stock).
Technology parameters: You can also adjust the feedrate and spindle RPM to suit the full cutting condi-
tions.
5 axes
Inclination strategy
Edge tilt angle: The tilt angle to the surface that should be achieved across the entire edge area. The
angle can be changed automatically to avoid collisions.
Macros
Shroud surface macro
Additional entry distance: Tangential extension of the entry movement.
hyperMILL
1378

-- 1378 of 1525 --

Link extension: The link extension defines the distance to the shroud surface where the infeed to the
adjacent toolpath (side infeed) occurs. In most cases, extremely small values suffice.
Hub macro
Start distance, Edge clearance: To exclude the hub fillets and the hub surface from machining, you can
raise the paths in the fillet area to a defined clearance area (1).
The paths are raised continually from a given start distance (2).
By reducing the feedrate, you can avoid potential tool overload caused by increased amounts of rest
material in the transition area.
Lift off paths
The empty lift off paths parallel to the cutting toolpath run at the level of the edge clearance. You can
adjust the feedrate for these paths to the empty cutting condition.

Check on: You must always enable this option if you want the tool to be checked for collisions. If the tool
check is not enabled, the tool used is shown in red in the graphic preview. When this check is enabled,
the defined clearance is used to check all of the components defined for the tool. We recommend that you
define the clearance so that it gets continuously larger, starting with the thick shank in the direction of the
spindle.
Tool check setup: the tool check settings are specified in this dialogue box. For further information, see
section Tool check setup (page 768)
Additional adjacent allowance: This parameter makes it possible to consider the additional allowance of
the possibly yet unmachined neighbour blade. Collisions with non-cutting tool elements can then be safely
avoided.
Edge tolerance: When using the Split paths and 4X machining options, you can define a separate toler-
ance for the collision check of the edge. This process allows for larger taper angles on the cutter.
Consider cutting edge: If this option is enabled, the tool cutting edge is considered in the tool check. For
blades lying extremely close together, it may make sense to disable this option.
Calculate length
The Reduce and Extend options are available if a holder, extension or spindle is defined. Only the Reduce
option is available for all 5X cycles.
Extend (1): if there is a tool extension, holder or spindle collision,
hyperMILL will calculate a larger tool
reach, based on the tool reach defined for the tool. So there is no limit to the maximum tool reach – the
maximum possible tool reach of a real tool is simply ignored! This is the preferred option if the selected
tool is available in different lengths (e.g., short, long, extra long) and the length calculation has not yet
determined the suitable real tool for the assembly. In this case, the tool is merely a geometry description
with an unlimited shank length.
Reduce (2):
hyperMILL calculates the shortest possible collision-free tool reach, based on the defined tool
reach of the tool. This is the preferred option if you only want to calculate tool lengths that are also actually
possible for the tool selected in the assembly. In this assembly, you must select the maximum tool reach
as the tool reach.

Display calculated tool length
If the same tool is used in several jobs, the tool length calculated by
hyperMILL is displayed. In this
instance, after creating the toolpath file(s), select the tool in the browser and choose the Usage function on

For unresolvable collision
Unresolvable collisions may occur if:
• It is not possible to avoid a collision in 5X machining as a result of a change to the tool orientation.
• In 3D machining, it is not possible to resolve a collision involving the tool extension, holder and/or
spindle by extending the tool (see calculating the tool length) or a collision will occur with the thick
shank.
If a collision cannot be avoided by changing the tool orientation (5X) or tool length calculation, various
options are available for the machining strategies:
Stop: The toolpath calculation stops when a collision occurs (applies for all machining strategies).
NC parameters
Machining tolerance: Enter the required machining tolerance. The value defines the accuracy with which
the calculation for the generation of the toolpath is carried out.
Maximum G1 length(1): maximum length of the G1 movements on planar surfaces which are output in
the NC program. Greater distances are subdivided into a corresponding number of G1 movements of the
specified length. Controlling the G1 length avoids too strong accelerations of the machine on large planar
surfaces.

1381

1
Machining angle tolerance: If both of the machine’s rotary axes are set relatively soft, the tool orientation
may deviate slightly from the collision-free orientation that has been calculated. To be on the safe side, you
can use this value to internally and conically enlarge the tool and holder by this angle.
Values that are too large will make it difficult to access the stock using thicker (more
robust) tools.
Max. angle increment: Restricts the permissible change of the tool inclination between two points.
Stop before execution: A stop marker in the toolpath causes the tool to stop.

-- 1382 of 1525 --

MB Fillet Milling
This cycle can be used to machine the fillets between the blade and hub surface.
Fillet milling is used to generate variable fillets or remove remaining rest material. This makes using larger
tools to mill blade and hub surfaces more effective.
Strategy
Milling reference
Main blade / Splitter blade: Specify the blade you want to machine. The selection of the splitter will not be
available, if it has not been defined on the geometry model.
Entry position
Due to the shorter distance from safety plane, it is better to use the leading side as the entry position.
On the splitter blade, the trailing side is better suited for use as the entry position as there is more space.
In the case of parts with splitter blades, we recommend you to use the same entry position (preferably the
trailing edge) for both blades.
Infeed strategy
Spiral down: Uniform spiral movements around the blade surface starting from the blade and moving in the
direction of the hub.
Spiral up: Uniform spiral movements around the blade surface starting from the hub and moving in the
direction of the blade.
Parameters
Blade limit:
Reference hub allowance: The blade limit is taken from the lateral position in the preceding hub finishing
job. The blade limit is calculated from the blade allowance used in that job.
The blade allowance for the current job should be identical to the one in the preceding hub finishing job.
Hub limit:
Reference blade allowance: The hub limit is taken from the axial position in the preceding blade machining
job. The hub limit is calculated from the hub allowance used in that job.
The hub allowance for the current job should be identical to the one in the preceding blade machining job.
Reference tool diameter: By entering the tool diameter used in the preceding machining jobs, it is possible
to calculate the amount of rest material in the corners.
Technology: Edge behaviour
You can define a local feedrate for both edges to prevent the rotary axes from acceleration too quickly
around these edges.
5 axes
Inclination strategy
4X Machining: Depending on the blade geometry, it may be possible to calculate a fixed tilt for the second
rotary axis. Access is then solely achieved by rotating about the Z axis.
Frame angle limitation
Max. angle to Z: The frame angle limitation prevents the system from calculating a tool orientation that the
machine cannot carry out.
Setup
Model
Specify the model (milling area) required for the current job.
For further information, see section Prepare manufacturing geometry (page 60).

13. OPEN MIND tool database
Please note that the demo data in the tool database is provided to illustrate the functionality of the system
only and is not for production purposes. OPEN MIND disclaims any liability for damages resulting from the
use of demo data in a production environment.
Database formats
As the MS Access ( .mdb) format does not support 64-bit technology, it has been changed to SQLite
( .db) with Version 2011. Please note that SQLite tool databases cannot be protected by passwords at
this time.
SQLite tool databases cannot be accessed by several users at the same time. This is only possible using
SQL Server technology, which is supported as of Version 2014.1.
SQL Server Native Client XX.X
If you are using SQL Server databases, ensure that you are also using an up- to-date
driver. The name of the driver must read: SQL Server Native Client XX.X.
Do not use drivers with the name SQL Server. This driver cannot transfer more than
400 kB of data to the server. As a result, you cannot use it to store 3D tools in your
database.
Convert older database to the new format
In order to use a database created under Version 2010 and older, you must convert it to the current
format. To convert an older database to the current format:
1. First, start your 2010 tool database from the Start menu under Start → Programs → OPEN MIND
→ Tool database [Version].
2. Open the database that you want to convert to the new format, select it in the browser and select
the Export → *.xml function from the shortcut menu by right-clicking. Your old database will be
saved in a Neutral tool exchange format that can then be imported with the tool database.
3. Now start your current tool database from the Start menu under Start → Programs → OPEN MIND
→ Tool database [Version].
4. Create a new (empty) database ( File → New) and under File type select the format Sqlite
database (.db).
5. In the browser, select the newly created database and then right-click to select the Import function
in the shortcut menu.
6. Then select the previously created file in the .xml format that you wish to convert to the new
format.
The Import status dialogue informs you about the current status of the data import.
Invalid lengths or duplicate designations are indicated in the Constraint Violation dialogue and must be
edited. Constraint violations can be resolved by different methods:
Automatic: All conflicts occurring during the import will be resolved automatically, so that all elements can
be imported from the old to the new database.
Ignore: Should only be used by experienced experts.
hyperMILL
1386

-- 1386 of 1525 --

The import continues even if there is no conflict solution. Since the application of this
option may result in faulty tools, it is only available if the options Leave, Overwrite and
OK are disabled.
The Leave/Leave All: The current element/all elements of the old database is/are preserved.
Overwrite/Overwrite All: The current element/all elements of the old database is/are overwritten with the
new element(s).
Deviation: The difference between the element of the old database and the element to be imported is
shown.
Database files in the *.mdb format will not be deleted after import to the current data-
base format but saved to your system in the same location under the name [ Daten-
bank_saved.mdb].
During the import, the tool heads defined in older versions are converted to tool spindles. Consequently, all
references are retained. However, the converted tool spindles are no longer displayed in the OPEN MIND
tool database. You can nevertheless use them when assembling a tool in
hyperMILL.
A database conversion is performed when importing tool data from an older version into the current format.
This operation should not be stopped, as otherwise
hyperMILL will not be able to load any data and joblists
and jobs will no longer be available.

the database browser.

and other version details.

window and in the graphical preview. If you have selected a folder, the elements of the folder are displayed
in a list view within the data view.

Right-click the upper area of the data view to configure the display of the parameters. Disable parameters
that are not to be shown in the data view.

type.
3. Click Create to create the database. The newly created database appears as an entry in the
browser.
You can use a password to protect database entries.

Allow plunge: Only available for Chamfered cutter. Enabled by default. The tool is allowed to plunge into

The Free tip geometry is not checked against collisions.

shank length.

Define turning tool
A turning tool is always constructed from the Insert and Tool holder components.
To define a turning tool:
1. On the Tools tab, right-click the corresponding database entry and select New → [Tool type].
2. Select or redefine the Insert and Tool Holder components.
A tool holder is made up of the shank geometry (part 1 and 2) and the extruded geometry. It contains all
placement information to support inserts.
By defining the Insert support you also set the Insert type to be supported by the tool holder, and via the
Clamping method, the manner in which an insert is to be mounted on the tool holder.
The Insert component is also characterised by geometric parameters as well as a Mounting type. In
addition, it is possible to assign to an insert the technology parameters Material, Cutter material and
Purpose.

area of the free form insert and confirm your definition with OK.
The Cutting area must match the contour that is to be processed.

ence point results from the Reference offsets X and Z.

Tool technology parameters
Technology data and cutting profiles allow you to create tools for special areas of use. If a tool is to be
used for finishing and roughing, define a corresponding Usage in the cutting profile and assign this to the
tool according to its use.
Technology data can be assigned either to Tools or Inserts. In doing so, the system differentiates between
milling and turning jobs. This means that individual technology data can take on different values for milling
jobs and turning jobs.
Define
To allocate technology parameters to a tool:
1. In the data view, click the Technology tab and set the Cutter material, Cutting edges and Spindle
orientation.
2. Then, in the lower area of the dialogue box select the required Material and Usage.
The technology data Cutting edges and Spindle orientation are available only for tools,
but not for inserts.
If an insert with defined technology data is assigned to a tool with technology parameters, the technology
data of the tool is overwritten with that of the insert.
You can define the following technology data:
Parameters Explanatory note
Material Define material
Cutter material Define cutter material
Usage Define technology usage
hyperMILL

Retract feedrate, Feedrate for retract movements (retract macro).

Feedrate retract Feedrate for retract movements (retract macro).

Infeed width factor (ae) / infeed length factor (ap): define a factor to modify the infeed width (ae) and infeed
length (ap) of holders, extensions and NC tools.
Maximum spindle speed/ Maximal feedrate: Limitation of feedrate and spindle RPM.
5X comp. length: Value for calculating the linear offset as a result of rotating the tool.
Max. angle for reduced feedrate: Maximum permitted angle of the surface to be machined for machining

(1) Surfaces, whose angle is smaller, are machined with feedrate XY.
(2) Surfaces, whose angle is the same or larger, are machined with the reduced feedrate.
Example: cycle: 3D Profile Finishing, Max. angle for reduced feedrate = 45°
Copy and insert
Copy technology data for tools and inserts.
Paste the copied technology data.
Pasting the copied data in the browser is possible for tools, inserts as well as folders on the Tools and
Inserts tab.
If technology data that is being inserted already exists, a prompt is shown asking you how you wish to
proceed regarding the existing data. Technology records are deemed to exist when both material and
usage match that of your entry.
The New, Overwrite and Keep options are available.
The New option is used to modify the new records depending on their insertion position such as to prevent
conflicts. When inserting on the Technology field (1), the new records are assigned a material that is not
yet being used. When inserting on the Material field (2), the new records are assigned a usage that is not
yet being used.
Use the Overwrite option to overwrite existing records. Records that do not already exist are inserted.
Use the Keep option to ensure that existing records remain unchanged. Records that do not already exist
are inserted.

For turning tool/drilling tool
Turning tool
• Retract feedrate: Feedrate used for retract movements. The Retract feedrate is used with the
Grooving cycle if the tool cannot move freely via the retract macro because of the model geometry,
but instead retracts along the material (1).
• Feedrate reduced: Feedrate for plunges into the material at a specific angle.
A distinction is made between the following application cases:
1. Turning, Axial, Radial and Contour parallel roughing strategy, the option Falling contours allowed
is enabled.
2. Feedrate reduced is always used when a combined X-Z movement occurs.
3. Grooving, strategy: Axial roughing with ramp. The ramping-in movement to the next infeed plane
always occurs in the Feedrate reduced mode.

Z+
1 2 	3
Drilling tool
The following applies to the drilling tool and boring bar tool types:
• Cutting speed (Vc) = m/min
• Fz drill (f) = mm/rev
• Spindle RPM (n) = Vc * 1000/pi * d
• Axial feedrate = Spindle RPM (n) * Fz drill (f)
The following applies to the tap drill tool type:
• Pitch = p
• Spindle RPM (n) = Vc * 1000/pi * d
• Axial feedrate = Spindle RPM (n) * Pitch (p)
Update
The Cutting speed (Vc), F/edge (fz) and Fz drill (f) technology data can be defined in the material dialogue
and in the data view of the tool (Technology tab).
In the material dialogue, if you set values for this technology data, define a new tool and assign a material
to it, the previously defined material technology data is linked to the tool technology data.
hyperMILL
1421

-- 1421 of 1525 --

This means that any change in the material technology data will be adopted automatically from the linked
tool technology data, including any necessary re-calculation of dependent values.
A linked value, then, can be modified on the tool technology data record only by one factor. The link can
be removed for each value individually. This way, the tool technology data remains unchanged in case of
changes to the material technology data.
Use standard formulas
1. In the Usage area, select the parameter.
2. Use the combo box to select the required formula.
The formula icon shows that the corresponding value has been defined using a
formula. This also applies to the data view of the NC tool.
For the Spindle RPM parameter, there is a formula for the Metric measurement system and one for the
Inch measurement system.
Define new formula
1. Right-click the database entry and select Formulas....
2. In the combo box in the Formula dialogue, select the area for which you want to define a new
formula.
3. Right-click in the Formula dialogue box and select New.
4. Enter a name for the new formula and double-click the Formula column.
5. Then, click the icon for displaying the formula elements.
6. Define the formula you require and select Ok to close the dialogue.
Formulas can be used in all numeric input fields.
Example: Diameter: (5+2)*3 = 21.
Only points, but not commas, are allowed, as decimal separators in formulas. Only
certain variables are allowed for formula definition, depending on the formula type. The
following restrictions apply: speed: spindle RPM (n) is not permitted. Length: ae, ap, fz,
z, Vc, n and f are not permitted. Feedrate: all variants are allowed.
The following mathematical functions are available for defining a formula:
Formula element Description
sin(x) Sine of X
cos(x) Cosine of x
tan(x) Tangent of x

2. Right-click and select New.
3. Enter the Name of the required material/cutter material and, if necessary, enter a suitable Com-

The name of the material/cutter material must be unique. Otherwise, you will get an
error message when you close the window.

1423

-- 1423 of 1525 --

Because the cutting conditions for the tool are largely affected by the cutter material, you can assign a
defined cutter material to each material in the cutter material dialogue.
Assign cutter material to a material
In the lower part of the Materials dialogue, you can assign each material one or more cutter materials.
In such an assignment, a distinction is made between the two measurement systems metric and inch as
well as between milling technologies and turning technologies.
Assign material to a cutter material
1. Select the material and then define whether the material-cutter material combination is to be used
as milling technology or turning technology with a metric or inch-based measurement system.
2. Click the icon and select the required cutter material from the list.
For each cutter material, you can define the Diameter limit, Cutting speed (Vc), F/edge (Fz) and Fz drill (f)
parameters as well as a measurement system.
Depending on the tool diameter, the F/edge (Fz) feedrate defined for the (upper) limiting diameter of the
cutter material and the cutting speed (Vc) are incorporated into the definition of the tool.
Example:
Material Cutter material Limiting diameter fz Vc
1.30255 (Al 99.5) SC (Solid Carbide) 10 0.3 250
1.30255 (Al 99.5) SC (Solid Carbide) 20 0.4 265
1.30255 (Al 99.5) SC (Solid Carbide) 30 0.6 280
Take technology parameters from cutter material for NC tool
To apply the F/edge (fz) and cutting speed (Vc) technology parameters from the cutter material definition
for an NC tool, follow the steps below:
1. Define a material and cutter material (including a limiting diameter, fz and Vc).
2. On the Tools tab, select the tool you require or define a new tool.
3. In the Technology area, select the relevant material and the associated cutter material and select
Standard as the purpose.
4. Based on the sample data contained in the above table, a defined tool diameter of 15 results
in the value 0.4 for the F/edge (fz) parameter and the value 265 for the Cutting speed (Vc)
parameter (see the table).
Define technology usage
Assign different technology parameters to a cutter material, depending on the machining (Roughing,
Finishing). This assignment is made in the data view of the tool definition in the technology parameters
area (Material > Cutter material).
To define a technology usage:
1. Select the database entry in the database browser and then select Technology Usages....
2. Right-click in the Technology Usages window and select New.
3. Specify the Usage and, if necessary, enter a comment.
hyperMILL
1424

-- 1424 of 1525 --

Save as default
To save a technology usage as a default:
1. Click the Technology tab of the tool’s data view.
2. In the lower area of the dialogue box, select the required Material and click the Usage entry.
3. Select the usage and then click the icon.
All of the technology parameters defined for this usage (including all of the formulas used) are saved as a
default.
If you then insert a new material in the data view of the tool, the parameters previously saved as a default
will always be used.
Define coolant
To define a new coolant:
1. In the database browser, select the required database.
2. Right-click and select the Coolant function on the shortcut menu.
3. The two coolants with the ID 1 and ID 2 are already predefined by default. Right-click and then
select New. Newly added coolants are numbered consecutively (ID 3, ID 4...).
4. If required, enter a Comment and select a Type for the coolant from the list.
You can define up to nine different coolants.
Assigning coolant to a usage
To assign a usage to a coolant:
1. In the data view of the tool, switch to the Technology tab.
2. Under Material → Usage → Coolant, click the icon and open the Coolant dialogue.
3. Activate the coolant intended for the usage.
The IDs of the activated coolants are displayed.
Define user-defined data class
1. Right-click the database entry and select Custom Data Classes....
2. Select the component for which you want to define the user-defined data from the selection list.
3. Right-click, select New and define the name for the data class (for example: Tool manufactur-
er, order number, storage location or similar).
4. If required, use a comment to describe the data class.
5. If required, use the icons to change the order of the entries.
6. Confirm your entries by clicking OK.
User-defined data classes are listed in the data view of the overview window on the
Geometry tab as Custom data. Each user-defined data class can be assigned a value
here (maximum 128 characters).

Create geometry with the geometry editor
Use the geometry editor to create freely definable geometries for tool components.
To do this, click the Geometry line in the data view of the component and then click the icon.
Specify a name for the geometry and define whether you want the geometry to be active and whether a
coupling exists.
To edit a geometry, click the icon and open the geometry editor.
Click the icon to delete a geometry.
Only one geometry can be active for each component. You cannot delete an active
geometry.
The geometry editor comprises an input area for defining line segments and a graphical preview (2D). To
add a geometry, right-click in the input area and specify the Height for the Origin and the Diameter and
Height for the line segment. Add a line segment using the Paste shortcut menu.
As the component geometries are always rotationally symmetrical models, you can
uniquely define a line segment by simply defining a Diameter and Height. The radius is
displayed in the graphical preview.
Component geometries must not contain any undercuts in the X direction.

Define NC tool
In the OPEN MIND tool database, a complete tool, which is used in machining, is referred to as an NC
tool. An NC tool always consists of the Tool component, however, a Spindle, Holder and Extension can be
defined as additional components.
To define an NC tool:
1. In the browser, switch to the NC tool tab.
2. Choose the database, right-click and select New → NC-Tool from existing tool... .
3. Select the tool you require in the Select tool dialogue and click OK to confirm.
Alternatively, proceed as follows to define an NC tool:
1. In the browser, switch to the Tool tab.
2. Select the Tool that is required to define the NC tool.
This function can also be used to create several NC tools at the same time. To
do this, simply select the required tools.
3. Right-click and select Create NC-Tool.
Define further parameters in the data view.
The data view of the NC tool is divided into the Geometry and Technology tabs. On the Geometry tab,
specify the general characteristics (NC number, Name) as well as the components that make up the NC
tool. On the Technology tab, define the material used and the cutter material, the usage as well as the
spindle speed and feedrates. If these have already been defined for the tool, they can be overwritten for
the NC tool.
Save NC tool as default
To save an NC tool as a default:
1. Select the required NC tool in the browser.
2. Right-click and select the Save As Default function on the shortcut menu. This will also save
reference points.
Assign a holder to several NC tools
To assign a holder to several NC tools at the same time, select the NC tools to which a holder is to be
assigned, select the Assign Holder function on the shortcut menu and select the required holder from the
list in the Select holder dialogue.
Components for NC tool
NC tools are assembled from the Spindle, Holder, Extension and Tool components in the data view of the
overview window.
To use components in the assembly:
1. Click the component or the icon in the data view of the Geometry area.
2. Select a spindle/a holder.
3. Select an extension.
4. Select a tool.
hyperMILL
1433

-- 1433 of 1525 --

5. Confirm the selection with OK .
When assembling an NC tool, the following conditions apply:
1. The measurement system of the selected tool determines the measurement system of the NC
tool.
2. All installed components must have the same measurement system.
If you assign a holder, extension or tool to an NC tool, only those components that
can actually be installed at the appropriate place are displayed in the relevant selection
dialogues.
To connect components with each other, you use couplings that can be categorised in the tool database
according to different basic types and can be installed according to classes.
The coupling types used and the size of each coupling (length, diameter) determine which components are
assembled together to form an NC tool.
If you use the holder or extension component when assembling an NC tool,
hyperMILL also checks the
maximum spindle RPM of the components and takes the lowest value for the NC tool.
Example
Holder 10.000
Extension 7.500
Tool 15.000
NC tool 7.500
To assign internal cooling to a component (holder, extension, tool holder), select the Internal cooling →
Yes option in the Technology area. If the coolant type for a Tool / NC tool is set to Internal cooling, all
components of the Tool / NC-Tool must also to be set to internal cooling.
The parameters on the tabs Geometry, Technology and Cutting point setup of the NC tool are described in
the following sections.
General parameters
The NC number (maximum: 10 digits) is transferred to the NC file and is used to identify the tool on the
machine that is used. For machines that can also evaluate non-numeric characters,
hyperMILL also allows
you to use an ID to define any combination of digits/characters (maximum: 32 characters) in order to
uniquely identify the tool.
The tool type and measurement system are taken from the selected tool.
Geometry parameters
(1) Spindle, (2) Holder, (3) Tool, (4) Clearance length, (5) Gage length, (6) Tool reach, (7) Tool length, (8)
Shank diameter, (9) Tip length, (10) Chamfer length, (11) Tool diameter, (12) Setting length z, (13) Setting
length x.

Technology parameters
To define technology parameters, switch to the Technology tab of the data view.
If Spindle RPM (n) and Feedrates have been defined for a material, they can be overwritten in the data
view of the NC tool and, if necessary, modified through the use of factors.
Tool reference: Either Tip or Centre can be set as the tool reference for the ball mill, bullnose end mill,
lollipop, woodruff, lens cutter and barrel tool types.
Tip (1): Z positions in the NC program are relative to the tool tip.
Centre (2): Z positions in the NC program are relative to the tool's centre point.
Reference points: Available for T-Slot Cutter, Drill Tool, Tap and and Boring Bar tool types. Any number
of reference points can be defined. Define Name and Position of the reference point.
Example: The value for the position of the reference point is based on the tool reference (1).
R1 Position = 2, R2 Position = -2.
A negative value for the reference point means that this point is moved two units in
a negative direction on the Z axis. At the same time, the clearance plane is aligned
accordingly.
An offset of 0 corresponds to the tool reference.
The tool reference must match the tool's measuring system and applies to all 5X and 3D jobs in a job list.
Factor speed / Faktor feedrate: The parameters can be defined irrespective of the material and they are
multiplied by the Spindle RPM (n) / Feedrate values.
The Factor speed parameter is also applied to the Cutting speed (Vc) during turning.
hyperMILL
1438

-- 1438 of 1525 --

Infeed width (ae) factor: Factor on the width of the tool tip used for cutting
Infeed length (ap) factor: Factor on the length of the cutting edge used for machining.
Maximal spindle RPM / Maximal feedrate: Limitation of spindle RPM and feedrate.
Factor values and Maximal spindle RPM / Maximal feedrate apply to the components Holder and Exten-
sion. Factor values are also applied to feedrates in the cutting profile if the feedrate unit is set to mm/rev or
inch/rev.
5X comp. length: Linear offset as a result of rotating the tool. The distance from the tool reference point to
the pivot point is normally composed of a tool-independent and a tool-specific part (comp. length).
Usable length: The following applies to drilling tools: Usable length = Cutting length - Tip length. The
following applies to tap drills: Usable length = Cutting length - Lead in length. The value can be modified
later on.
The following apples to all other tool types: The Usable length (5) is determined based on the Tool
diameter (1), Tip length (2), Tip angle (3) and Section (4) parameters. Tip angle (3) and Lead in length (4)
are calculated based on factor values.
For milling tools the following also applies: Usable length = Tip length.
If the tool reach is lower than the tip length, the usable length corresponds to the cutting length.

Define depot
Use depots to clearly group and administer tools according to your own criteria.
To define a depot:
1. Go to the Depots tab in the database browser.
2. Right-click the database entry, select New → Depot and specify a Name and, if necessary, a
Comment (tooltip) for the depot.
3. Enable the Contains NC tools option if you want the depot to contain NC tools.
To create a new depot within an existing depot:
1. Select the relevant depot and right-click.
2. Select New → Depot.
Save NC tool in a depot
To save an NC tool in a depot:
1. Select the relevant depot and right-click.
2. Select New → Depot item...
3. In the Select NC-Tool dialogue, select the tool you require and confirm your selection with OK.
Alternatively, proceed as follows:
1. Select the required tools on the NC tool tab.
2. Select the Create Depot Items... function from the shortcut menu.
3. In the Select Depot dialogue box, select the depot you require and confirm by selecting OK.
The NC tools are now available in the depot and the parameters are displayed in the data view. If some of
the NC tools already exist in this depot, they are not added and a corresponding message is displayed.
The Create Depot Items.. function is also available for entire folders. This allows you to
transfer the content of an entire directory to a depot.
If NC tools are contained in a depot, they are identified by the following general parameters: Alternative
NC-Number, Alternative ID and Alternative NC-Name. The parameters initially correspond to the NC-Num-
ber, ID and Name parameters.
You can change the alternative parameters manually. If you create a depot as a magazine, for example,
the Alternative NC-Number can be used as the place number of the tool. This number therefore always
needs to be unique.
Transfer NC tool from depot to
hyperMILL
If you transfer tools from a depot directly to
hyperMILL, the Alternative NC-Number is transferred as the
Number and the Alternative NC-Name as the Name in the tool browser.
To transfer a depot or individual tools from a depot to
hyperMILL:
1. Select the required entries, right-click and
2. select Transfer to hyperMILL.

Data exchange
A neutral format ( *.xml) is available for exchanging data with other tool databases.
You can import or export both an entire database and individual folders or elements.
For more information on the XML data exchange format, please contact your OPEN MIND partner.
Importing/exporting data
1. Select the required database entry in the database browser.
2. Select Import / Export on the shortcut menu.
3. Then choose Neutral Tool Exchange Format *.xml for file type.
Please note: The Import shortcut menu function is only available for database nodes.
Importing data via drag-and-drop: You can easily import tool and technology data using
drag-and-drop. This is done by dragging the .xml file from the file explorer to the
desired database node in the file browser. This function is available for all tool data that
was previously exported from the tool database in
hyperMILL .xmlformat, as well as for
tool manufacturer data that can be saved in
hyperMILL .xml format.
Export folder structure
To export just the folder structure of your OPEN MIND tool database:
1. Select the element you require (database or individual folder) in the database browser and
2. select the Export structure option on the shortcut menu.
Synchronise data
To synchronize tool data of a supported tool management system with the OPEN MIND tool database,
proceed as follows:
1. In the database browser, select the database into which you want to import the data of another
system.
2. Choose Synchronization... in the context menu of the database entry. The OPEN MIND tool
database synchronisation service dialog opens.
3. With Input format optionally define the format of the data to be imported. The neutral data
exchange format of OPEN MIND (.xml) is used by default. If Prserve folder structure is activated,
the folder structure of the data is not changed during the import. The function is only available for
the neutral data exchange format from OPEN MIND.
4. For Database select the database into which tools from the other system are to be imported,
i.e. the database used for synchronization. If the dialog is opened from the tool database, the
database for which the dialog was opened is already entered.
Activate the Child database option, if this database should be "read-only". Only the synchroniza-
tion service can then write to the database, so that accidental changes are prevented.
5. For Data exchange folder select the folder where to which the tool management system
exports tools.
6. Control the data exchange in the Service area. The Start buttonstarts the data exchange, to end
click on the Stop button. For Log file select a folder in which the log file with information about
synchronization is saved and define a name for the log file.
7. Click Close to close the dialogue.
hyperMILL
1447

-- 1447 of 1525 --

Command line functions for synchronization
The synchronization of the OPEN MIND tool database with one of the supported tool management
systems can also be controlled via the command line. To start the synchronization service, call the
file omTdbService.exe. This file is located in the OPEN MIND installation directory under Tool Data-
base\[version]. The following functions are available:
/i[nstall] Installs and starts the service.
/r[emove] Stops and uninstalls the service.
/h[elp] Shows this message.
/f[older] P Absolute path to the folder where the tool management system exports tools to.
/d[atabase] D Database in which to import tools from the other system.
/t[ype] T Optional import format type. The following format types are supported:
std: Expects XML files using the OPEN MIND neutral data exchange format.
tdm: Expects files in the format as they are delivered by products of TDM Systems
GmbH. If not given, std is assumed.
/p[reserve] Preserve folder structure. Only supported if format type is std.
/s[lave] Marks the database as read-only Slave database. Accidental data changes are
prevented.
/polling-time T The service uses folder change notifications to get informed when to start synchro-
nizations. But after some time of inactivity it looks itself at the folder for changes.
The time of inactivity can be controlled by T (in seconds - 60 = default).
/reset-slave Resets the Slave database flag of the given database. This should only be used if
the service fails to reset the flag in the database.
Example for a command to install and start the synchronization service:
"C:\Program Files\OPEN MIND\Tool Database\[version]\omTdbService.exe" /i /d "C:\da-
tabase\my_sql_server_tdb.dns" /f "C:\database\import"
This command line starts the service for the server database, that is specified
in my_sql_server_tdb.dns and expects the files of the tool management system
underC:\database\import.

Additional functions
Sort tools / NC tools
Tools can be sorted either By name or By diameter. NC tools can be sorted By NC number or By diameter.
To do this, select the required database or folder in the database browser and use the Sort function on the
shortcut menu.
Create reports
Generate report files with the parameters of the defined tools and/or tool components. You can generate
reports for tools, NC tools, extensions, depots and holders.
To create a report:
1. Select the element you require in the browser (you can also make multiple selections).
2. Right-click and
3. select Report... from the shortcut menu .
The data is initially temporarily saved in the *.html format and displayed in your default browser. You can
now back this data up anywhere on your system.
The creation of reports can be controlled from the Options → General menu.
Show report after generation
The generated report file is opened automatically in the default program.
Overwrite report output directory
When creating a new report, an existing report directory is deleted and a new directory is created. By
default, reports are saved in the [tooldbReport] directory of the Global working space. If you use
project paths, they are saved to the [tooldbReport] directory of the project path defined.
For information on creating reports, see section ReportDesigner (page 1491).
Specify accuracy
You can specify the accuracy for both the metric and inch measurement systems, as well as separately for
angles and factors.
1. Right-click the required database in the database browser and
2. select Accuracy from the shortcut menu.
3. Specify the corresponding accuracies for the measurement system used and for the angle and
factor.
4. Alternatively, you can also specify the accuracy via the Options → Accuracy menu.
Specify measurement system
1. Right-click the required database in the database browser and
2. select Measurement system → Metric / Inch from the shortcut menu.
Change password
1. Right-click the database entry in the database browser and
2. select Change password from the shortcut menu.
3. Enter the old password, then specify the new password.
4. Confirm the new password.

Showing properties of the tool database
1. Right-click the required database in the database browser and
2. select Properties... from the shortcut menu.
The following properties are displayed: File name, User, Version and URL.
Multiple selections
Select multiple elements in the browser at the same time. To do this, click to select the required elements
and hold down the CTRL key at the same time. Depending on the type of elements selected, different
functions are available in the shortcut menu (right-click) (including Copy/ Export).
You can also use the multiple selections function to transfer several tools to
hyperMILL. For further
information, see section Import tool from database (page 56).
Copy & Paste
In the browser of the OPEN MIND tool database, move or copy elements to a different place in your
database using drag-and-drop operations.
To move an element, select the required element with the left mouse button and move it to the required
location while holding down the mouse button.
To copy an element, hold down the CTRL key at the same time. This function is available both for
elements and for folders.

Interfaces
Interfaces to the following tool management systems are supported in the OPEN MIND tool database:
• TDM Systems (page 1451)
• WinTool (page 1451)
• Zoller (page 1452)
• NCSIMUL | Tool (page 1452)
TDM Systems integration
Manage the exchange of data with the TDM Systems tool management system using the TDM Systems
integration.
Set up the TDM Systems database from the following dialogue: hyperMILL → Setup → hyperMILL →
settings → Database → Settings Wizard.
Import tools from the TDM Systems database
1. Open the TDM Systems database
via the hyperMILL → Tools → Import TDM Systems tools entry or
via the job definition, job browser or tool browser.
2. Click a tool icon to first select the required tool type and then the tools to be imported.
If the TDM Systems database was opened from the job dialogue, then only the tool type already
selected in the job dialogue is selectable.
Tools which were imported using the TDM Tool Manager can be used in macro pro-
gramming. A prerequisite is that the tools are saved in the database as an NC tool with
a unique ID. In the Apply macro dialogue, NC tools used in macro jobs which come from
the tool database and have a unique ID are marked as DB.
Export tools to the TDM Systems database
1. Open the TDM Systems database via the menu hyperMILL → Tools → TDM Systems tools.
2. Define the name of the tool list to be exported using List ID.
Either all local tools defined in the ( *.hmc) model file are exported or all tools in a job
list. To only export the tools in a job list, select the respective job list beforehand.
WinTool integration
The WinTool integration enables data exchange with the WinTool tool management system and is availa-
ble via the hyperMILL → Tools menu.
It is possible to access complete tools and tool lists directly from
hyperMILL. The tools exported from
WinTool are not written to the OPENMIND tool database, but directly to the
hyperMILL document. This
way, a redundant tool management system is avoided.
To enable the WinTool integration, right-click the CAD program’s toolbar and select WinTool hyperMILL
Interface.
hyperMILL
1451

-- 1451 of 1525 --

Import tools from the WinTool database
During the exchange of data between WinTool and
hyperMILL, the existing tool IDs are checked. When
importing tools from WinTool,
hyperMILL assigns NC numbers automatically. The next NC number is the
highest existing number + 1.
Export tools to the WinTool database
Using the WT-MakeList function, all tools used in a hyperMILL document are adopted in a list and
exported to WinTool. The list consists of a set of IDs and NC numbers for each tool used.
For more information on the functions of WinTool integration, see your WinTool documentation.
Zoller integration
The Zoller integration enables data exchange with the Zoller tool management system and is available via
the hyperMILL → Tools menu.
Import tools from the Zoller database
Open the Zoller database dialogue to choose the tools that are to be imported to
hyperMILL. The
imported tools are automatically entered in the tool list of the current document.
Export tools to the Zoller database
All tools used in the document are exported to the Zoller database. If the document contains multiple
job lists, a usage list is created for each job list of the document
Import and export are available only if the Zoller TMS has been started.
Only
hyperCAD 2009.3: Optionally, display the buttons for the interface. To do this, right-click the
toolbar, use the Adjust function to open the Toolbars dialogue and enable the Zoller TMS hyperMILL
option.
NCSIMUL | Tool
The NCSIMUL | Tool integration enables an exchange of data with the NCSIMUL | Tool tool management
system and is available via the hyperMILL → Tools menu.
Import tools from the NCSIMUL | Tool database.
Open the NCSIMUL | Tool database dialogue to choose the tools that are to be imported to
hyperMILL.

14.
hyperVIEW
hyperVIEW’s basic functions include:
• Display of the toolpaths and control of the tool's movements.
• Machine simulation based on toolpaths.
• The generation of NC files.
• The generation of reports.
• Print functions.
This documentation provides you with:
• A brief overview of the basic functions in the following section.
• Information on the screen layout in section User interface (page 1455).
• A brief summary of the most important workflows in section Important workflows (page 1456).
• Detailed descriptions of the individual functions on the menu in section Menu functions (page 1460).
• Descriptions of the
hyperVIEW browser functions in section Functions in the hyperVIEW brows-
er (page 1466).
• Information on the toolbars in section Toolbars (page 1487).
User interface
The user interface consists of the following elements:
(1) Menu bar, (2) Toolbars, (3) Browser, (4) Graphics area, (5) Status bar.
hyperMILL
1455

-- 1455 of 1525 --

Important workflows
Important workflows are outlined below.
Set up machine
For much of the work carried out, you need to specify a machine to use for simulations. Therefore, when
you start
hyperVIEW for the first time, you will be prompted to set up a machine.
Proceed as follows to set up a machine:
1. Open the Machine administration dialogue.
2. Alternatively, open the Machine administration dialogue via the job list in
hyperMILL ( Postproces-
sor → Machine).
3. Specify the machine's name and postprocessor in the Common category of the Machine proper-
ties dialogue.
The postprocessor's parameters need to be suitably configured before it is used for the
first time. Please contact your OPEN MIND dealer to get information regarding this.
Proceed as follows to modify a postprocessor's configuration:
1. Open the Postprocessor configuration dialogue and, if necessary, change the name, type and
value of individual parameters.
2. Make sure to document all changes made in the configuration dialogue!
Model mode: Specify whether a machine model is to be used for the simulation or whether only the part
and tool are to be displayed. If a machine is used, define the format of the machine model file.
Model from MMF file / VMM file: Select if a machine is to be displayed in
hyperVIEW.
Select the machine model file. The settings for Model from VMM file correspond to the settings for the
Fixed part option.
Model from postprocessor: Select if the postprocessor ( *.oma) contains a machine model. Only licensed
tool machine models can be used. For more information on this, please contact your OPEN MIND partner.
Please note that these machine models are not assured to match any particular ma-
chine in your machine shop. Functions like collision control and workspace monitor may
vary from our typical model to your actual machine. OPEN MIND or your OPEN MIND
partner can adjust the machine to your particular requirements. This service, which
does not form part of the standard delivery, is charged separately.
Fixed part / Fixed tool: Select if there is no machine model or if the machine model is irrelevant to the
simulation. Only the part and the tool are displayed in the simulation; one of the two needs to be fixed.
Generate NC program
Proceed as follows to write an NC file:
1. Define machine.
2. Create an NC job (right-click > Create NC job).
hyperVIEW creates an entry in the browser
consisting of the following elements: machine, several parts (stock, model, result) and toolpaths.
hyperMILL
1456

-- 1456 of 1525 --

3. Insert a toolpath (select the Toolpath entry in the browser, right-click and select > Insert toolpath).
4. Start the postprocessor run (select the NC job entry, right-click and select > Write NC-File).
The postprocessor run terminates with an error message if no licence is found.
OPEN MIND has enhanced the postprocessor run to include an analysis of the postpro-
cessor. The following message appears if a security-related issue is detected:
Important note on your postprocessor. OPEN MIND detected a security issue. Please
contact your OPEN MIND business partner.
Set up machine simulation
Proceed as follows to set up the machine simulation:
1. Define machine.
2. Create an NC job and insert toolpath.
3. Define the machine simulation conditions. To do this, switch to the Simulation tab in the browser
and specify the required settings.
Machine origin: If you select the Automatic option, the parts used and the toolpaths will
be positioned automatically. Use Machine Setup to define other origins.
Animation control
C: All tool movements of the respective job are simulated.
G1: Only tool movements on the G1 plane are simulated.
G0: Only tool movements on the G0 plane are simulated.
If you set the (Program) halt option to On, the simulation will be stopped at the point specified in the NC
file.

Generate report
Generate a report for tool lists, job lists or statistical information (tool movements, dwell times, coolants
and so on) in the formats *.htm, *.rtf, *.txt and *. xml (for Excel 2002).
Proceed as follows to create a report:
1. On the File menu, select the Report entry or select the NC job entry in the browser, right-click and
select the Report option.
2. In the Report dialogue, select the required format and a template file.
3. Specify a path and file name and save the file.
For the generated report file to open automatically, you need to select the Show report after generation
option on the Options → General menu.
Reports including statistical evaluations can only be created if in
hyperMILL (job definition > General
dialogue page) the Generate NC file option is enabled.
Use a text editor to customise script files ( *.JLR) for modifying the content of report files according to
your individual requirements.
Print information
Print information on the NC file, machine, tool parameters or machining cycles for an NC job.
Define print layout
To define the print and CSV layout:
1. On the Options menu, select the Print and CSV Layout entry.
2. Select the <new layout> option and specify a name.
3. Define the printing values (double-click the Available values column).
4. Use the arrow keys to specify the order of the values.
5. Click OK to confirm the print and CSV layout.
Print
To print the layout:
1. Select Print from the File menu.
2. In the Print dialogue, define the printer, print area and layout.
3. Click OK to close the Print dialogue.
To print out NC jobs, the browser window needs to be active, as otherwise the current contents of the
graphics window will be printed instead.
CSV format: The defined parameters are saved in a text file with comma separators between the values.
hyperMILL

This format enables further editing in a spreadsheet program such as Excel.
To generate a file in *.CSV format:
1. Select CSV from the File menu.
2. Select the storage location, file name, file type and layout.
3. Click Save to close the dialogue.
Menu functions
File
Open: Open files in the format *.hv or *.hvz. When you open *.hvz files, the files contained in the
archive are unpacked to a temporary directory ( tmp).
This automatically deletes all browser entries.
Append: Appends the selected file ( *.hv / *.hvz) underneath the last browser entry. Existing entries are
not deleted.
Save as: Save a file in the format:
*.hv: With this file type, information about the machine, stock, model and toolpaths is linked to an NC job.
All of the NC jobs in the browser are saved.
This gives you the option of saving a project (NC file) even if you haven't yet defined all the areas. Missing
data can still be added at a later point.
*.hvz: All of the files associated with a project file (*.hv) are saved together in a ZIP file with the following
file structure:
NC-Job X
- 3DF/
- POF/
- STOCK/
- NC/
NC-Job Y
With postprocessor: Include the postprocessor in the .hvz file. This includes all *.def files that are
located in the same directory as the postprocessor ( .oma file).
With machine model: Include the machine model in the .hvz file.
The options are important for the OPEN MIND support team and are enabled by default.
Unpack Archive: Unpack all the files associated with the project file (that is also contained in the ZIP
archive) to the selected directory.
Report: Open the Report dialogue. It is possible to output tool lists, statistical evaluations and job list
reports; to some extent also with a graphical representation of the toolpaths. The following file formats
are available: HTML, RTF, TXT and XML (Excel 2002). Select the file type and report required, confirm
your selection by clicking OK and then enter the path and file name to save the report file. A report file is
generated for every NC job in the browser.

General
Toolpath
Dim inactive toolpaths in highlight mode: Controls the display of the toolpaths in highlight mode (shortcut
menu: Highlight mode). If this function is enabled, all unselected toolpaths are dimmed.

function is disabled, all unselected toolpaths are hidden.

dialogue box).

The Coordinate systems shortcut menu lists all the coordinate systems of the current NC job including
origin and reference system.
The report file that is generated only contains information on the selected NC job and
the selected toolpath. The printout lists information on all of the NC jobs contained in the
browser.
In addition, you can list individual statistics for each toolpath, such as: length of movement in G0, G1,
G2/G3, dwell times and the number of tool changes.
Feedrate Analysis
The feedrate values of the calculated toolpaths are displayed using different colours. This allows for an
easier and faster check of the toolpaths and the feedrates selected or calculated. Particularly during High
Performance roughing, the realised feedrate adjustment can be checked and reproduced easily.
Displayed range: Change the largest or smallest feedrate displayed manually or
with the arrow keys.
The colours used for each feedrate area are displayed in the colour scale.
Toolpaths with only one feedrate value are shown in red. Feedrates outside the
displayed range are shown in white.
Select Reset to restore the original values.

Job mode
One NC file per job: Select this option if a separate NC file is to be generated for each toolpath. Otherwise,
all toolpath files will be written to a single NC file during the postprocessor run. The job name or job list
name is used here. If a separate NC file is written for each toolpath, the rule for file name generation is
applied when the respective NC file is generated.
Compound job as single job: A separate NC file is generated for a compound job.

fined parameters for the job list name, job name, job ID and counter are also available.
Start of counter: The generated files are numbered consecutively, beginning with the first number specified
(n; n+1; n+2).

Program halt
Enter commands in the NC file that trigger a program halt at critical points.

Commands: Enter the commands you want to insert in the NC file.
NCS transformation
Define a predetermined offset for the NCS. First, the rotation is executed, followed by the displacement.
Thus, a displacement refers to the rotated NCS. A warning is issued in this context when loading data in
hyperVIEW and during the postprocessor run.
Select the Enabled checkbox to turn the NCS transformation on. X offset moves the NCS in the direction
of the X axis, Y offset in the direction of the Y axis and Z offset in the direction of the Z axis. A value must
be entered for the required distance. Rotary axis determines the axis of the NCS around which the NCS is
to be turned. Rotation angle defines the value for the rotation. It is applied only if the rotation axis has the
value x, y or z.

to enable it. Tolerance and colour can be specified for each individual option. All other information, such as
machine, stock and so on, are taken from the first NC job in the
hyperVIEW browser.
Machine simulation
Collision check mode: Only available with a standard postprocessor. Use the Off, On and Head against

Off: The movements between the machine components arenot checked for collisions.

Tool spindle alignment
Arbitrary tool spindle alignment: When this option is enabled, the tool spindle angle is not checked during
the postprocessor run.
When the option is disabled, the tool spindle alignment is checked during the postprocessor run in relation
to the orientation of the X axis of the job frame. If the tool spindle alignment deviates, a message appears,
indicating by how many degrees it deviates.
In the context of performing back boring actions, this function is used to check whether
the alignment of the tool spindle of turning tools is identical to the alignment of the X
axis of the job frame before the tool moves eccentrically into and out of the hole.
